teile.einleitung: The **whitefish** (Felchen) is a silvery fish that lives in many Swiss lakes. For commercial fishing in Switzerland it is the most important fish, and it often ends up as a fillet on the plate.
wichtigste: The whitefish is the most important fish for commercial fishing in the Swiss lakes.
Whitefish belong to the salmon family.
They live in large, cool and clean lakes.
Depending on the region, they are also called Balchen, Albeli or Renken.
Whitefish eat mainly tiny creatures in the water, the **plankton**.

abschnitte.text: Whitefish are slender, silvery shining fish. They belong to the **salmon** family. They are found in many large lakes in Switzerland, for example Lake Constance, Lake Lucerne or Lake Geneva. They need cool, clean, oxygen-rich water. Mostly they swim in shoals in open water and eat **plankton**, that is, tiny creatures that float in the water.

For **commercial fishing** in the Swiss lakes, the whitefish is the most important fish. The fishermen catch it mainly with **nets** from a boat. To maintain stocks, young whitefish are raised in fish hatcheries and released into the lakes. Whitefish are popular because their flesh is tender and has few bones. They are often eaten fried as a fillet.

In almost every large lake, separate forms of whitefish have developed that differ in size and way of life. Experts count many different species in Switzerland. That is why there are also many names: **Balchen**, **Albeli**, **Gangfisch** or **Renken**. When lakes contain too many nutrients, oxygen becomes scarce. Then the whitefish decline, and some species have even died out in the past.

gewusst: In some Swiss lakes several species of whitefish live side by side, staying at different water depths.

teile.einleitung: The figure of the Earth describes the shape and size of the Earth. The Earth is almost a sphere but is slightly flattened at the poles. Even in ancient times scholars knew that it is round.
wichtigste: The circumference at the equator is about **40,000 km**.
The diameter measures about **12,700 km**.
From pole to pole the Earth is about 43 km shorter than at the equator.
**Eratosthenes** calculated the Earth’s circumference astonishingly accurately around 240 BC.
The surface is about **510 million km²**, and about 71 per cent of it is water.
The shape of the mean sea surface is called the **geoid**.

abschnitte.text: That the Earth is round was already known in ancient times. The philosopher **Aristotle** noticed that the Earth’s shadow in a **lunar eclipse** is always round. Around 240 BC **Eratosthenes** even calculated the Earth’s circumference. He compared the angles of the Sun’s shadows in Alexandria and Syene in Egypt. From the difference in angle and the distance between the two cities, he arrived at an astonishingly accurate value.

The circumference at the equator is about **40,075 km**. An aeroplane at 900 km/h would need almost two days for it without a break. The **diameter** at the equator measures about 12,756 km. The whole **surface** covers about 510 million km², of which about **71 per cent** is covered with water.

The Earth turns fast on its axis. As a result it is pushed slightly outwards at the **equator** and slightly **flattened** at the poles. From pole to pole its diameter is therefore about 43 km shorter than at the equator. That is why the summit of **Chimborazo** in Ecuador, almost on the equator, is the furthest from the centre of the Earth. It reaches further into space than Mount Everest, although it is lower above sea level.

The Earth is not entirely regular. The masses inside the Earth are unevenly distributed, so **gravity** is not equally strong everywhere. The shape that follows the mean sea surface is called the **geoid**. Shown greatly exaggerated, it looks like a slightly dented potato. For maps and heights, experts calculate with a simplified shape, an **ellipsoid**, as does the national survey of Switzerland at swisstopo.

The first voyage right round the Earth was achieved by the expedition of **Ferdinand Magellan**. He set off in 1519 with five ships from Spain but died in 1521 in the Philippines. **Juan Sebastián Elcano** brought the last ship back to Spain in 1522. This proved that you can sail round the whole Earth.

gewusst: The highest point above the sea is Mount Everest, but the peak furthest from the centre of the Earth is Chimborazo.
The metre was originally defined so that the distance from the North Pole to the equator is exactly 10 million metres, which is why the Earth’s circumference is almost exactly 40,000 km.

teile.einleitung: Germany is the neighbouring country to the north of Switzerland and the most populous country in the European Union. The capital is Berlin, and the country consists of 16 federal states. From the Alps in the south to the North Sea and the Baltic in the north, the landscape is very varied.
wichtigste: Germany lies north of Switzerland.
The capital and largest city is Berlin.
Germany has 16 federal states.
The highest mountain is the Zugspitze at 2,962 metres.
About 83 million people live in Germany (as of 2024).
Germany has been reunified since 3 October 1990.
Germany is a founding member of the European Union and pays with the euro.

abschnitte.text: Germany lies in the middle of Europe and borders nine countries, more than any other country in Europe. In the south it borders Switzerland at **Lake Constance** and on the Rhine. In the north lie the flat North German Plain and the coasts of the North Sea and the Baltic. Right in the south the Alps rise up, with the **Zugspitze** as the highest mountain.

For a long time the territory consisted of many small kingdoms and principalities, and a German nation state only came into being in 1871. After the Second World War, Germany was divided in 1949 into two states, the Federal Republic in the west and the GDR in the east. From 1961 the **Berlin Wall** divided the city of Berlin. It fell in 1989, and on 3 October 1990 Germany was **reunified**.

Germany is a **federal state** with 16 federal states, similar to Switzerland with its cantons. The largest cities are Berlin, Hamburg, Munich and Cologne. Berlin, Hamburg and Bremen are so-called city states, that is, cities that are themselves a federal state. Near Switzerland lie cities such as Konstanz, Freiburg im Breisgau and Lörrach.

Germany has the largest economy in Europe. It is known for cars, machinery, chemicals and electrical engineering. For Switzerland, Germany is the most important trading partner. Many people from Germany live and work in Switzerland, and thousands commute across the border every day.

The official language is **Standard German**, and there are also many dialects, for example Bavarian or Swabian. The Alemannic spoken in southern Baden is closely related to Swiss German. Famous Germans include the poet Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, the composer Ludwig van Beethoven and the physicist Albert Einstein. Einstein also lived in Switzerland for a long time and developed important ideas in Bern.

The **Brandenburg Gate** in Berlin is a symbol of reunification. The fairytale castle of Neuschwanstein in Bavaria is visited by over a million people every year. Cologne Cathedral is one of the largest churches in the world. The Danube rises in the Black Forest.

begriffe.erklaerung: A constituent state of Germany, similar to a canton in Switzerland.
The joining together of West and East Germany in 1990.
A state made up of several constituent states with their own rights.
German Democratic Republic, the East German state from 1949 to 1990.

gewusst: With nine neighbouring countries, Germany has more neighbours than any other country in Europe.
At Lake Constance, Germany, Austria and Switzerland meet.

teile.einleitung: A thunderstorm is a weather event with lightning and thunder, often accompanied by heavy rain, wind and hail. In Switzerland there are thunderstorms mainly on hot summer days.
wichtigste: Thunderstorms form in tall, thick storm clouds.
A lightning bolt is a huge electrical spark.
After the lightning you hear the thunder.
If you count the seconds between lightning and thunder, you can estimate how far away a thunderstorm is.
In a car you are well protected in a thunderstorm.
Under a single tree and in water it is dangerous.

abschnitte.text: On hot days, warm, moist air rises quickly. There it cools and huge, tall clouds form. Experts call these **storm clouds** cumulonimbus. They can reach over ten kilometres high and look flat like an anvil at the top. In the clouds, ice grains and water drops collide, and **electrical voltage** builds up.

When the voltage becomes too great, it discharges in a **lightning bolt**. A lightning bolt is a huge **electrical spark** between a cloud and the ground or between clouds. It heats the air very strongly in a flash. The air expands abruptly as it does so, and we hear this as **thunder**. If lightning strikes a dry tree, it can start to **burn**.

abschnitte.titel: How far away is the thunderstorm?
abschnitte.text: Light is much faster than sound. That is why you see the lightning first and hear the thunder only afterwards. If you count the **seconds between lightning and thunder**, you can estimate how far away the thunderstorm is. About three seconds correspond roughly to one kilometre. When you hear the thunder, the storm is already close enough to be dangerous.

You are safest in a **house** or in a **car**. The metal of the car carries the current around the outside of the occupants into the ground. Never stand **under a single tree**, because lightning likes to strike tall things. If you are swimming in a lake or a swimming pool, get **out of the water** at once. Outdoors you should avoid summits, ridges and open ground.

In Switzerland there are thunderstorms mainly in summer, often in the afternoon or evening. They are especially frequent in the Pre-Alps, in the mountains and in Ticino. In the mountains, thunderstorms can build up very fast, so the weather forecast is important before a hike. **MeteoSwiss** issues warnings for severe thunderstorms with hail and gusts of wind.

gewusst: A lightning bolt can briefly heat the air to about 30,000 degrees, which is hotter than the surface of the Sun.
Hailstones form in storm clouds when ice grains are swirled up and down several times and grow as they do so.

teile.einleitung: The Föhn is a warm, dry wind that blows down the slopes in the Alpine valleys. In Switzerland almost everyone knows it: it brings clear views, but sometimes storms too.
wichtigste: The Föhn is a warm, dry downslope wind.
It forms when air flows over the Alps.
It is well known, for example, in the Reuss Valley and in the Rhine Valley.
In Föhn conditions the mountains look clear and close.
Föhn makes snow melt quickly and can make fires dangerous.
Typical are lens-shaped clouds, the “Föhn fish”.

abschnitte.text: In a Föhn, air flows against the **Alps** and has to rise. As it does so it cools, and clouds form. On this side it often rains or snows. On the other side the **air sinks into the valley**. As it sinks it is compressed and warms up. Because it has already lost its water, it arrives **warm and dry**.

The Föhn blows mainly in the **Alpine valleys**. It is well known, for example, in the **Reuss Valley** and in the **Rhine Valley**. When the air comes from the south, it is called a south Föhn. But there is also a north Föhn, which blows on the southern side of the Alps. The Föhn can reach **storm force** and knock trees down.

Föhn air is very dry and clear. The mountains therefore seem **especially close** in a Föhn. In the sky you often see smooth clouds in the shape of a lens. They are called **Föhn fish** or lenticular clouds. Some people feel unwell or get a headache in a Föhn.

In spring the warm Föhn makes the **snow melt quickly**. That is why it is sometimes also called the “snow eater”. The dry, strong wind can also spread a **fire** quickly, though. For this reason lighting fires outdoors is often forbidden in a Föhn. In earlier times whole villages burned down in Föhn valleys.
In Switzerland and Germany the **hairdryer** is also called a “Föhn”. It blows warm air like the Föhn wind. This is where the name comes from. The wind and the device are spelled the same.

gewusst: In a strong Föhn in winter, it can be clearly warmer in an Alpine valley than on the lowland plains.
The word Föhn goes back to the Latin word “favonius”, meaning a mild west wind.

teile.einleitung: Ghana is a country in West Africa on the Gulf of Guinea. It used to be a British colony and in 1957 became one of the first countries south of the Sahara to gain independence.
wichtigste: The capital of Ghana is Accra, and the official language is English.
Ghana used to be called the Gold Coast and was a British colony.
Ghana became independent in 1957, and its first president was Kwame Nkrumah.
A lot of cocoa for chocolate is grown in Ghana.
Lake Volta is a huge reservoir.
In the middle of the flag there is a black star.

abschnitte.text: **Ghana** lies in West Africa on the coast of the **Gulf of Guinea**. The capital is **Accra**, a big city right by the sea. **English** is the official language, and many African languages are spoken as well, for example Twi. The flag has the colours red, yellow and green. In the middle there is a **black star**, a sign of the freedom of Africa.

abschnitte.titel: The Gold Coast and colonial times
abschnitte.text: In 1482 Portuguese sailors built the fortress of **Elmina** on the coast. Later, more European traders came. Because of the large amount of gold, the Europeans called the area the **Gold Coast**. For centuries, people were also taken from here to America as slaves, and the old fortresses are a reminder of this. From the 19th century the Gold Coast was a **British colony**.

In 1957 the country became **independent** and took the name **Ghana**, after an old African empire. Ghana was one of the first countries south of the Sahara to break free from a colonial power. The independence movement was led by **Kwame Nkrumah**, who became the first prime minister and later the first **president**. A well-known Ghanaian was also **Kofi Annan**, who was Secretary-General of the UN.

The **Ashanti** people had a powerful kingdom in the interior of the country. Its most important symbol is the **Golden Stool**. It is considered sacred and the seat of the soul of the whole people. Nobody is allowed to sit on it. To this day there is a king of the Ashanti, who plays an important role in culture and tradition.

Ghana is one of the biggest **cocoa** producers in the world. Cocoa trees grow on many small farms, and chocolate is made from their beans. Swiss chocolate also contains cocoa from West Africa. In the east of the country lies **Lake Volta**, one of the largest reservoirs in the world. It was created in the 1960s when the River Volta was dammed with the Akosombo Dam.

gewusst: The Akosombo Dam on Lake Volta supplies a large part of the electricity in Ghana.
Kente cloth from Ghana is a brightly woven fabric that is worn at festivals.

teile.einleitung: Dubai is the largest city in the United Arab Emirates and lies on the Persian Gulf. In a few decades a small trading town became a world city with skyscrapers, artificial islands and a huge airport. Dubai is also the name of one of the seven emirates.
wichtigste: Dubai is the largest city in the United Arab Emirates.
The emirate is ruled by the Al Maktoum family.
The inlet Dubai Creek divides the old town into Deira and Bur Dubai.
The Burj Khalifa was the tallest building in the world in 2025.
In 1966 oil was found off Dubai.
Because the oil reserves are small, Dubai relies on trade, tourism and finance.
In the south lies the large port of Jebel Ali with a free trade zone.

abschnitte.titel: From fishing town to world city
abschnitte.text: In the past, people in Dubai lived from fishing, trade and **pearl diving**. The historic core lies on **Dubai Creek**, an inlet that divides the old town into **Deira** and **Bur Dubai**. On the Creek, small wooden boats called abras still carry people from one bank to the other. The emirate is ruled by the ruling family **Al Maktoum**. The capital of the United Arab Emirates, however, is Abu Dhabi.

In **1966**, **oil** was found off the coast of Dubai. This brought a lot of money for the expansion of the city. The oil reserves are, however, **relatively small** compared with neighbours such as Abu Dhabi. Dubai therefore relied early on **trade, tourism and finance**. In the south, the large port of **Jebel Ali** was built with a free trade zone, where companies from all over the world work.

The **Burj Khalifa** is 828 metres high and in 2025 was the **tallest building in the world**. It opened in 2010. Another landmark is the luxury hotel **Burj al Arab**, which looks like a billowing **sail** and stands on its own small island. Off the coast the artificial island of **Palm Jumeirah** was built up in the shape of a palm tree. Hotels and villas stand on it.

Dubai’s airport is among the busiest in the world. The airline Emirates is based here, and many travellers change planes on their way to Asia or Africa. The city has a driverless **metro**. People from very many countries live in Dubai, and most residents do not come from the Emirates. In 2021 and 2022 the **World Expo** took place here.

Dubai lies in a **desert**. In summer it is often over 40 degrees, and it rains very rarely. Drinking water is mostly obtained from seawater by removing the salt. Many buildings, shopping centres and even bus stops are air-conditioned. Critics point out that this way of life uses a great deal of energy.

gewusst: In a shopping centre in Dubai there is a ski hall with real snow, in the middle of the desert.
From the Burj Khalifa you can see the sunset twice: first at the bottom and, after a quick lift ride, again at the top.

teile.einleitung: A **Fata Morgana** is a mirage that deceives our eyes. In the desert people then think they see water in the distance, although there is only hot sand.
wichtigste: A Fata Morgana is a trick of the eyes caused by a mirage.
It arises when light is bent in warm and cold layers of air.
In the desert, the blue sky is often reflected and looks like water.
Here too in summer, such reflections can be seen on hot roads.
If you walk towards the apparent lake, it moves back or disappears.
A Fata Morgana can be photographed, because the light really is there.

abschnitte.text: Anyone travelling through the desert on a hot day sometimes sees a glittering **lake** in the distance. But if you walk towards it, it moves back or disappears completely. What you see is in reality a reflection of the **blue sky**. Because it shimmers and flickers, our brain takes it for water. In the past this often led travellers in the desert astray.

A Fata Morgana needs **hot air** directly above the ground and cooler air above it. Light travels at different speeds through warm and cold air. At the boundary of the air layers it is therefore **bent**, which experts call **refracted**. A ray of light from the sky makes a curve in this way and enters our eye from below. We therefore see the sky where the ground actually is.

A Fata Morgana does not occur only in the desert. In summer, on a hot **road**, you often see apparent puddles in which cars are reflected. When you come closer, the road is dry. Because the light really does fall into our eye in this way, a Fata Morgana can even be **photographed**. Over cold water there are also inverted reflections, in which ships or coasts seem to float in the air.

The name comes from Italian and means “Morgan le Fay”. This **fairy** appears in old legends, including the stories about King Arthur. It was believed that she could conjure up illusions in the air with magic. Such appearances became particularly well known in the **Strait of Messina** between Italy and Sicily, where people sometimes thought they saw cities above the sea.

gewusst: A Fata Morgana is no dream and no imagination, because a camera records it too.
In some reflections, islands or ships seem to hang upside down above the horizon.

teile.einleitung: The Ganges is one of the largest rivers in Asia. It flows through the north of India to Bangladesh and is a sacred river for Hindus.
wichtigste: The Ganges rises at a glacier in the Himalayas.
The largest part of the river lies in India.
In India it is called Ganga, and many say “Mother Ganga”.
For Hindus the Ganges is sacred.
Together with the Brahmaputra it forms the largest river delta in the world.
In the delta lie the mangrove forests of the Sundarbans with the Bengal tiger.

abschnitte.titel: From the Himalayas to the sea
abschnitte.text: The **Ganges** rises at a **glacier** in the **Himalayas**, the highest mountain range in the world. Then it flows through the wide plain in **northern India**. It is about 2,500 kilometres long. At the end it reaches **Bangladesh**. Together with the **Brahmaputra** it runs into the **Bay of Bengal** there.

In India the river is called **Ganga**. Many also call it **“Mother Ganga”**. For followers of **Hinduism** the Ganges is sacred. Many bathe in it because they believe the water cleanses the soul. At great festivals millions of pilgrims come to its banks.

One of the best-known cities on the Ganges is **Varanasi**. It is one of the oldest cities in India. On the bank, broad flights of steps, the **ghats**, lead down to the water. There people pray, bathe and celebrate. For Hindus, Varanasi is an especially sacred city.

abschnitte.titel: The largest delta in the world
abschnitte.text: The Ganges and the Brahmaputra together form the **largest river delta** on Earth. It lies mainly in Bangladesh. On the coast grow the **Sundarbans**, one of the largest **mangrove areas** in the world. The **Bengal tiger** lives there. It can swim well.

In the Ganges lives a special mammal, the **Ganges river dolphin**. The river water is murky, so it can **hardly see**. It finds its way by **echolocation**: it sends out clicking sounds and listens for the echo. The Ganges river dolphin has become rare. The **pollution** of the river is also a big problem.

gewusst: At the confluence of the Ganges and the Yamuna, one of the largest religious festivals in the world takes place, the Kumbh Mela.
The Ganges river dolphin is the national aquatic animal of India.

teile.einleitung: **Fold mountains** form when huge forces inside the Earth push layers of rock together until they fold like a tablecloth. The Alps and the Jura are well-known examples right on our doorstep.
wichtigste: Fold mountains form through the squeezing together of layers of rock.
The upward-arched part of a fold is called an **anticline**, the downward-arched part a **syncline**.
The Alps formed when Africa pushed against Eurasia.
Large rock masses that have been moved far are called **nappes**.
The Jura is a young fold mountain range and gave the Jurassic its name.
The Urals are an old, heavily eroded fold mountain range.

abschnitte.text: The Earth’s crust consists of large **plates** that move very slowly. When two plates collide, the layers of rock in between are squeezed together. They do not always break but often bend into **folds**. The upward-arched part is called an **anticline**, the downward-arched part a **syncline**. Over millions of years, whole mountain ranges rise in this way.

The Alps formed when the **African Plate**, with a spur, the **Adriatic Plate**, pushed against **Eurasia**. In the process, huge masses of rock were pushed over each other. These **nappes** shape the structure of the Alps. The rock at the summit of the **Matterhorn** belongs to the Adriatic Plate, so it comes originally from the African side. In the Alps you also find **ophiolites**, remains of former oceanic crust of a vanished sea.

In the cantons of Glarus, St Gallen and Graubünden lies the **Sardona Tectonic Arena**, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. There you can see a clear line on the rock faces, the **Glarus Main Thrust**. Above this line, older rocks lie on younger ones. This shows that whole masses of rock were moved far. At the **Tschingelhörner** lies the well-known **Martinsloch**, through which the Sun shines twice a year onto the village of Elm.

The **Jura** is a young fold mountain range in north-west Switzerland and in France. It gave the **Jurassic** period of Earth history its name. In the **Folded Jura**, the cover of sediments slid off on soft **layers of salt and gypsum** from the Triassic and lay down in folds. Quite different are the **Urals** in Russia: they are an old fold mountain range from the **Palaeozoic**. Wind and water have worn them down strongly over a very long time, so they are much lower today than the Alps.

gewusst: The Himalaya is still growing today, because India keeps pushing against Asia.
On high Alpine summits, fossilised sea creatures are found, because these rocks once lay on the seabed.

teile.einleitung: Gold is a shiny, yellow precious metal that people have wanted for thousands of years. It is used for jewellery, coins, bars and even in electronics.
wichtigste: Gold stays shiny even when it lies in the air for a long time.
A cast block of gold is called a gold bar.
Gold is mined in a gold mine or washed out of river sand.
In 2024, China produced the most gold.
Switzerland has no big gold mines, but it is one of the most important countries for refining gold.
From 1848 there was a famous gold rush in California.

abschnitte.text: **Gold** is a precious metal with the chemical symbol **Au**, from the Latin word “aurum”. It is very heavy and soft. What is special is that gold **does not rust** and does not tarnish. Even when it lies in the air or in water for a long time, it **stays shiny**. It can be hammered into wafer-thin sheets, called **gold leaf**.

Gold is used mainly for **jewellery**, for example rings and necklaces. A lot of gold is also cast into **gold bars** and kept by banks or private individuals as an investment. Because gold conducts electricity well and does not rust, small amounts of it are also found in mobile phones and computers. In sports competitions you get a **gold medal** for **first place**. However, it is usually made only partly of gold.

Gold is mined from the rock in a pit, a **gold mine**. In 2024 **China** produced the most gold, followed by countries such as Russia and Australia. Small grains of gold can also be found in river sand. In **gold panning**, you swirl sand and water around in a pan. The heavy gold stays at the bottom, and the light sand is washed away.

Switzerland has no big gold mines. Even so, it is one of the most important countries for **refining** gold. In big refineries, mainly in Ticino, gold from all over the world is cleaned and cast into bars. If you want to look for gold yourself, you can pan for gold in the **Napf region** between Bern and Lucerne. There you can find tiny flakes of gold in the streams.

In 1848 gold was found in **California**, on the land of the Swiss emigrant **Johann August Sutter**. Soon tens of thousands of people streamed in from all over the world to get rich. This is called the **gold rush**. Many gold seekers, however, found hardly anything. Sutter himself lost a large part of his property because of the rush.

gewusst: All the gold ever mined would make a cube only a little over 20 metres on each side.
From one gram of gold you can draw a very long wire as thin as a hair.

teile.einleitung: The **Everglades** are a huge subtropical wetland in the south of Florida in the USA. Rare animals and plants live here, and part of the area has been a national park since 1947.
wichtigste: The Everglades are a large subtropical wetland in Florida.
The large lake Lake Okeechobee feeds the Everglades with water.
Since 1947 part of the Everglades has been a national park.
Alligators and crocodiles live together here, which hardly happens anywhere else.
The introduced **Burmese python** is now a big problem.

abschnitte.text: The Everglades look like an endless meadow of tall **sawgrass**, but beneath it stands shallow water. This water flows very slowly from **Lake Okeechobee** south to the sea. That is why the Everglades are also called the “river of grass”. In between lie small islands with trees, and on the coast dense **mangrove forests**. The climate is warm and humid, with a rainy season in summer.

The Everglades are the only known place where **alligators** and **crocodiles** occur together. Alligators like fresh water, while crocodiles live more in the salty water on the coast. Where fresh and salt water mix, they meet. **Manatees** also live here, many water birds such as herons and spoonbills, and the rare **Florida panther**.

A big problem is the **Burmese python** from South-East Asia. People kept the snakes as pets and released some of them. Today very many pythons live in the Everglades. They eat birds and small mammals, whose numbers have fallen sharply as a result. People are therefore trying to catch the snakes and slow their spread.

Since 1947 part of the Everglades has been a **national park**. In the past large areas were drained to make room for fields and cities. Canals diverted a lot of water, and the swamp shrank. Today there are large programmes to restore the natural flow of water. The national park is also a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

gewusst: In the Everglades, visitors often travel in airboats that glide over the shallow water.
Through the groundwater, the Everglades supply a large part of the drinking water for southern Florida.

teile.einleitung: The flag of Canada is one of the best-known flags in the world. In its middle shines a red maple leaf, which stands for the whole country.
wichtigste: The flag shows a red maple leaf on a white field.
On the left and right it has a red stripe each.
The maple leaf has eleven points.
Canada has had the maple leaf flag since 1965.
On 15 February, Canada celebrates the day of its flag.
Many Canadians call their flag “The Maple Leaf”.

abschnitte.text: The flag is twice as wide as it is high. It consists of three vertical fields: on the left and right a **red stripe** each, and in the middle a **white square**. In the white field stands a red **maple leaf**. The leaf is drawn in simplified form and has exactly **eleven points**. Red and white are regarded as Canada’s national colours.

Canada was closely tied to Britain for a long time. Earlier flags therefore showed the British **Union Jack**. In the 1960s the government wanted a flag of its own that stands only for Canada. After long discussions in Parliament, the maple leaf flag was chosen. On **15 February 1965** it was officially raised for the first time.

The **maple** grows very commonly in Canada, above all in the east of the country. Long before 1965 the maple leaf was a popular symbol of Canada. In autumn the maple forests turn **red and orange**. This play of colour attracts many tourists every year. From the sap of certain maple trees the well-known **maple syrup** is also boiled.

Every year on **15 February**, Canada remembers the introduction of its flag. This day is called “National Flag of Canada Day”. Many people simply call their flag **“The Maple Leaf”**. The name Old Glory, by contrast, belongs to the flag of the USA. In Switzerland the great national day is 1 August.

gewusst: The maple leaf can also be seen on Canadian coins.
Canada has two official languages, English and French. The flag does without writing and so suits both.

teile.einleitung: On 6 February 2023 two very strong earthquakes shook the south-east of **Turkey** and the north of **Syria**. They destroyed many cities, and it was one of the worst natural disasters in this region for a long time.
wichtigste: The first main quake occurred at **4:17 a.m.**
It had a **magnitude of 7.8**.
About 9 hours later a second quake with a magnitude over 7 followed.
The quakes occurred on the **East Anatolian Fault**.
The series of quakes is often named after the province of **Kahramanmaraş**.
In total about **60,000** people died.
The **Swiss Rescue Chain** sent a team to Hatay Province.

abschnitte.titel: In the middle of the night
abschnitte.text: The first quake struck people in their sleep at **4:17 a.m.** local time. The epicentre lay near Pazarcık in the province of **Kahramanmaraş**, which is why people also speak of the Kahramanmaraş earthquake. With a **magnitude of 7.8**, it was one of the strongest quakes in Turkey since measurements began. Many people were buried in their homes, and there was bitter **winter cold**.

What happened in the afternoon was especially unusual. About **9 hours** after the first quake, an independent quake of magnitude 7.5 to 7.7 followed near **Elbistan**. It occurred on a neighbouring fault. Buildings that the first quake had damaged now collapsed, and the destruction became much greater still.

From the south the **Arabian Plate** presses north against Eurasia. As a result the **Anatolian Plate**, on which a large part of Turkey lies, is squeezed out sideways to the west. At the **East Anatolian Fault** the blocks of rock slide past each other sideways, which is called a strike-slip fault. In 2023 the rupture extended over about 350 km.

About 59,000 to 62,000 people died, of them over 53,000 in Turkey and several thousand in Syria. The historic city of **Antakya**, ancient Antioch, was devastated over a large area, and old churches and mosques also collapsed. A building amnesty of 2018 was strongly criticised afterwards: at that time owners could have unapproved buildings legalised for a fee. Critics saw this as a reason for poor earthquake safety.

Many countries sent rescue teams. The **Swiss Rescue Chain** sent 87 specialists with **search dogs** to Hatay Province. It includes, among others, the federal government’s SDC, the association **Redog** with its rescue dogs, and rescue troops of the army. The teams searched the rubble for survivors.

gewusst: That two quakes with a magnitude over 7 occur on the same day in the same region is very rare.
The Swiss Rescue Chain is organised so that it can fly out quickly after a request from abroad.

teile.einleitung: The Dominican Republic lies in the Caribbean on the island of Hispaniola, which it shares with Haiti. The country is known for beaches, baseball and merengue. Its capital, Santo Domingo, is the oldest city in the Americas founded by Europeans.
wichtigste: The capital is called Santo Domingo.
The country shares the island of Hispaniola with Haiti.
The official language is Spanish.
Pico Duarte is the highest mountain in the Caribbean.
Baseball is the most popular sport.
The dance merengue comes from the Dominican Republic.
A Bible can be seen in the coat of arms on the flag.

abschnitte.titel: A country on a divided island
abschnitte.text: The Dominican Republic lies on the island of **Hispaniola** in the Caribbean. It takes up the larger, eastern part, and to the west lies **Haiti**. Christopher Columbus reached the island in 1492, and afterwards it became a Spanish colony. That is why the official language is **Spanish**. In 1844 the country became independent. The currency is called the peso.

The capital, **Santo Domingo**, was founded by Spaniards at the end of the 15th century. It is the **oldest European city in the Americas** that is still lived in today. In the old town, the Zona Colonial, stand the first cathedral in the Americas and other very old buildings. The old town is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.

The country has not only beaches but also high mountains. At about 3,100 metres, **Pico Duarte** is the **highest mountain in the Caribbean**. In the Dominican Republic a lot of **cocoa** is grown, from which chocolate is made, along with sugar cane, bananas and coffee. Only here is the pale blue gemstone **larimar** found, whose colour recalls the sea.

The most popular sport is **baseball**. Many players in the North American professional league come from the Dominican Republic. The dance **merengue**, with its fast, cheerful rhythm, also comes from the country. It is part of UNESCO’s intangible cultural heritage. The music **bachata** also began here.

The flag shows a white cross that divides it into blue and red fields. In the middle sits the **coat of arms**. On it an open **Bible** can be seen, with a small cross above it. The Dominican Republic is one of the few countries with a Bible on its flag. The motto on the ribbon is “Dios, Patria, Libertad”, that is, God, Fatherland, Liberty.

gewusst: In larimar you can sometimes see fine white patterns that look like waves on the sea.
Columbus called the island “La Española”, and from this came the name Hispaniola.

teile.einleitung: The hawksbill turtle is a sea turtle that lives in tropical seas, especially in coral reefs. It has a pointed mouth like a bird’s beak and a beautifully patterned shell. Unfortunately it is now seriously endangered.
wichtigste: The hawksbill turtle lives in warm, tropical seas.
In the coral reefs of the Caribbean it eats mainly sponges.
Its mouth is pointed and recalls a bird’s beak.
Its shell used to be made into tortoiseshell.
The species is regarded as critically endangered.

abschnitte.text: The **hawksbill turtle** lives in tropical parts of the Atlantic, the Pacific and the Indian Ocean. It likes best to stay in **coral reefs** and on rocky coasts. Its head is narrow, and the mouth tapers to a point like a **beak**. The shell consists of horny plates patterned in brown, yellow and black, which overlap at the edge like roof tiles.

In the reefs of the **Caribbean**, the hawksbill turtle eats mainly **sponges**. Many sponges contain hard, needle-like particles or even poisonous substances. They hardly bother the hawksbill turtle, however. With its pointed mouth it can also get at sponges in narrow gaps between the corals. It also eats jellyfish, algae and other small animals. In this way it helps to stop the sponges from overgrowing the corals.

From the horny plates of the shell, **tortoiseshell** used to be made, a material for combs, spectacle frames and jewellery. For this reason very many animals were hunted. Today international trade in tortoiseshell is banned by the **Washington Convention on endangered species**. Even so, the species is regarded as **critically endangered**. To protect it, beaches where the females lay their eggs in the sand are guarded.

gewusst: The newly hatched young look for the way to the sea at night, guided by the light above the water.
Anyone who buys tortoiseshell souvenirs on holiday may not bring them into Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Earth’s orbit is the path on which the Earth circles the Sun once a year. It is almost a circle, but not quite: for this reason the Earth is sometimes a little nearer to the Sun and sometimes a little further away.
wichtigste: The Earth needs one **year**, about 365.25 days, for one round of the Sun.
The orbit is a slight **ellipse**.
The Earth is nearest to the Sun at the **beginning of January**.
It is furthest away at the beginning of July.
The average distance is about 150 million kilometres.
The Earth moves at about **30 km per second**.

abschnitte.text: The Earth’s orbit is an **ellipse**, that is, a slightly stretched circle. The astronomer **Johannes Kepler** found this out about 400 years ago. In the case of the Earth, the ellipse is stretched so little that you would hardly see the difference from a circle by eye. The average distance to the Sun is about **150 million kilometres**. This distance is also called an **astronomical unit**.

abschnitte.titel: Near in January, far in July
abschnitte.text: The point nearest the Sun is called **perihelion**. The Earth reaches it around 3 January at a distance of about 147 million kilometres. It reaches the point furthest from the Sun, the **aphelion**, at the beginning of July at about 152 million kilometres. This shows that the seasons do not come from the distance to the Sun, since for us it is winter in January. They arise from the tilted **Earth’s axis**.

On its orbit the Earth covers on average about **29.8 kilometres per second**. That is over 100,000 kilometres per hour, much faster than any rocket at launch. We feel nothing of this because everything on Earth moves along with it, including the air. When it is near the Sun in January, the Earth is a little faster than in July.

abschnitte.titel: A year and the leap day
abschnitte.text: For one whole round, the Earth needs a little more than **365 days**, namely about 365 days and 6 hours. So that the calendar does not slip, almost every four years there is an extra day, **29 February**. Such a year is called a **leap year**.

gewusst: In a single year the Earth covers almost a billion kilometres on its orbit.
In the northern hemisphere, winter is slightly shorter than summer, because the Earth moves faster when it is near the Sun.

teile.einleitung: An iceberg is a large piece of ice that has broken off a glacier and floats in the sea. Usually you see only a small part of it, and the largest part lies under water. Icebergs can be huge and become dangerous for ships.
wichtigste: Almost the whole iceberg lies under water, and only about a tenth sticks out.
Icebergs are made of fresh water.
They float because ice is lighter than water.
When an iceberg breaks off a glacier, this is called calving.
In Antarctica there are flat, wide tabular icebergs.
The Titanic sank in 1912 after a collision with an iceberg.

abschnitte.text: Glaciers consist of snow that was pressed together into ice over many years. An iceberg is therefore made of **fresh water**, although it floats in the salty sea. Where a glacier reaches the sea, large pieces break off and plunge into the water. This process is called **calving**. Most icebergs in the **North Atlantic** come from the **glaciers of Greenland**.

Ice is somewhat **lighter than water**, which is why an iceberg floats. But only a small part, about a tenth, sticks out of the water. **Almost all of it** lies below the surface. This is where the expression “only the tip of the iceberg” comes from, when you see only a small part of something. When an iceberg drifts into **warmer sea**, it slowly **melts**.

In **Antarctica**, huge plates of ice push out over the sea, the **ice shelves**. When pieces break off them, **tabular icebergs** form. They are flat and wide like a table. One of the largest icebergs ever observed was called **B-15**. It broke off the Ross Ice Shelf in **2000** and was bigger than the canton of Graubünden.

Because the largest part of an iceberg cannot be seen, it is dangerous for ships. In **1912** the **Titanic** collided with an iceberg on her first voyage and sank. More than 1,500 people lost their lives. Afterwards the **International Ice Patrol** was founded. It still watches the icebergs in the North Atlantic today and warns ships. Today aircraft, radar and satellites help with this.

gewusst: The ice in an iceberg can be thousands of years old. Tiny air bubbles from earlier times are trapped in it.
When an iceberg melts, it sometimes crackles, because the old air bubbles burst.

teile.einleitung: The Gulf of Guinea is a large bay of the sea on the west coast of Africa. It belongs to the Atlantic Ocean and is important for fishing, shipping and oil production.
wichtigste: The Gulf of Guinea belongs to the Atlantic Ocean.
In the gulf the equator and the prime meridian cross.
The Niger forms a huge delta there.
In the Niger Delta and off the coast, mainly oil is produced.
In the gulf lie the island state of São Tomé and Príncipe and the island of Bioko.
For years, piracy has threatened ships in the Gulf of Guinea.

abschnitte.text: The **Gulf of Guinea** is a large bay of the **Atlantic Ocean** on the west coast of Africa. It stretches from Ivory Coast to Gabon. Along its coast lie countries such as **Ghana**, Togo, Benin, **Nigeria** and **Cameroon**. Its easternmost part, off Cameroon, is called the **Bight of Biafra**, and further west lies the Bight of Benin.

In the Gulf of Guinea there is a special point: here the **equator** and the **prime meridian** **cross**. This point therefore has the coordinates 0° latitude and 0° longitude. It lies in the middle of the sea, far from any coast. On maps and in computer programs it sometimes turns up when a place is missing and is wrongly set to zero as a result.

In the gulf there are several volcanic islands. On the island of **Bioko** lies **Malabo**, the capital of **Equatorial Guinea**. The rest of this country lies on the mainland. Further south lies the small island state of **São Tomé and Príncipe**. It consists of two main islands and is one of the smallest countries in Africa. It used to be a Portuguese colony.

The great **River Niger** flows into the gulf and forms a huge **delta** with many river branches and mangrove forests. In the Niger Delta and off the coast, mainly **oil** is produced. For Nigeria, oil is one of the most important sources of income. At the same time, leaks and oil spills pollute water and soil, and the people of the region suffer from this.

For years, **piracy** has threatened ships in the Gulf of Guinea. Armed groups attack cargo ships and tankers. The countries of the region work together and send patrols out to sea to make shipping safer. International navy ships also help with this.

gewusst: Map experts jokingly call the point at 0° latitude and 0° longitude “Null Island”, although there is no island there at all.
The Niger Delta is one of the largest river deltas in the world.

teile.einleitung: Deforestation means that forests are cut down or burned and not replanted. Tropical rainforests are especially affected. This has consequences for animals, plants, the weather and the climate.
wichtigste: In the Amazon region, most forest is cleared for **cattle pasture**.
In Indonesia and Malaysia, **oil palms** are pushing out a lot of rainforest.
In South America, **soya** is grown as animal feed on cleared land.
In **slash-and-burn**, forest is burned down.
When trees are burned or rot, **CO2** is released.
Without forest, it can rain less in the Amazon region.
The **FSC label** stands for wood from responsibly managed forests.

abschnitte.text: In the **Amazon region**, most of the cleared area is used as **pasture** for cattle. On other areas, **soya** is grown, which is very rich in protein and is fed to chickens, pigs and cattle worldwide. In Indonesia and Malaysia there are now huge **oil palm plantations** where rainforest once stood. Palm oil is obtained from their fruit, and it is found in many foods and cosmetics.

In **slash-and-burn**, trees are felled or set alight directly in order to gain arable or grazing land. The ash fertilises the soil only for a short time. After that the soil is often poor in nutrients, and new forest is cleared. The smoke from the fires can envelop whole regions.

Trees store **carbon** in wood and leaves. When they are burned or rot, this carbon enters the air as **CO2** and strengthens the greenhouse effect. Trees also release a lot of water into the air through their leaves. A large part of the rain in the Amazon region comes from this **evaporation**. Without the forest, fewer clouds form, and it becomes drier.

In the tropical rainforest, especially many **species** live in a small space. Many animals and plants are found only there. When the forest is destroyed, they lose their **habitat** and can die out. People who live in and from the forest also lose their home.

abschnitte.titel: What can be done about it
abschnitte.text: With **satellite images**, the rainforest is photographed regularly from space. Brazil analyses them to spot new clearing quickly. When shopping, labels help: the **FSC label** of the Forest Stewardship Council shows that wood or paper comes from a forest managed according to rules for the environment and people. In **Switzerland** a law has protected the forest since the 19th century, and anyone who clears forest must as a rule create a replacement.

gewusst: The forest area of Switzerland has been growing for many decades, because the forest is strictly protected here.
The Amazon rainforest produces a large part of its rain itself, through the water its trees evaporate.

teile.einleitung: The Gobi is a large desert in Asia that stretches across Mongolia and the north of China. It is mainly a desert of stones and rubble, with very hot summers and icy winters.
wichtigste: The Gobi Desert lies in Asia, in Mongolia and China.
In Mongolian the name roughly means “waterless place”.
High mountains hold back the rain clouds, so little rain falls.
Winter in the Gobi is very cold.
Researchers found famous dinosaur eggs in the Gobi.
Bactrian camels, wild camels and the rare Gobi bear live there.

abschnitte.text: The **Gobi** lies in Central Asia, in the south of **Mongolia** and the north of **China**. It is one of the largest deserts on Earth. The name comes from Mongolian and roughly means **“waterless place”**. Unlike what you might think, only a small part of it is made up of sand dunes. Mostly you see stones, rubble and sparse grass.

The climate in the Gobi is extreme. In summer it can get very hot, but **winter** is **very cold**, with temperatures far below zero. Rain falls only rarely. The reason is the **high mountains** such as the Himalayas and the Tibetan Plateau to the south. They hold back the damp rain clouds before these reach the Gobi. This is called a **rain shadow**.

The Gobi is famous among researchers for its **fossils**. In the 1920s an American expedition discovered **dinosaur eggs** there. This was a sensation, because at that time hardly anyone knew of such eggs. Since then many more dinosaurs have been found in the Gobi, for example Velociraptor and Protoceratops. The rocks there are particularly well preserved.

Animals that can cope with dryness and cold live in the Gobi. The **Bactrian camel** is a camel with **two humps**. It is kept as a domestic animal by the nomads. The **wild camel**, by contrast, still lives wild in the desert and is very rare. Even rarer is the **Gobi bear**, a kind of bear that occurs only in the Gobi. Only very few of these bears are left.

Many people in the Gobi live as **nomads**. They travel with their herds of sheep, goats, horses and camels from pasture to pasture. They live in **yurts**, round tents made of a wooden frame and thick felt covers. A yurt can be put up and taken down quickly. The felt keeps you warm in winter and cool in summer.

gewusst: On the edge of the Gobi, grazing land keeps turning into desert, which is called desertification.
The place where the famous dinosaur eggs were found is called the “Flaming Cliffs” because of its red rocks.

teile.einleitung: The Statue of Liberty stands in New York harbour and is a landmark of the USA. It was a gift from France and in the past welcomed many immigrants who arrived by ship.
wichtigste: In English it is called the “Statue of Liberty”.
It stands on Liberty Island, a small island in New York harbour.
In its raised hand it holds a torch.
Its skin is made of thin copper that has turned greenish.
Gustave Eiffel built the iron framework inside.
It was dedicated on 28 October 1886.

abschnitte.text: France gave the statue to the USA as a sign of friendship. It was designed by the French sculptor **Frédéric-Auguste Bartholdi**. The supporting **iron framework** inside was built by **Gustave Eiffel**, who later put up the Eiffel Tower in Paris. The statue was brought to America in parts by ship. On **28 October 1886** it was solemnly dedicated.

In its raised right hand the statue holds a **torch**, a sign of the light of freedom. On its head it wears a **crown of rays** with seven spikes. In its left arm it holds a tablet with the date **4 July 1776**. On this day the USA declared its independence. That is why 4 July is the national holiday there.

The outer skin consists of thin **copper plates**. At the beginning the statue gleamed copper-red like a new coin. Through air and rain, a greenish layer, the **patina**, formed over time. It protects the metal underneath. That is why the statue is **greenish** today.

The statue stands on **Liberty Island**, a small island in New York harbour. You can reach it only by **boat**. As far as the **crown** there is no lift. You climb up a narrow **spiral staircase** with many steps. From there you can see over the harbour and the skyscrapers of Manhattan.

gewusst: At the feet of the statue lie broken chains, a sign of the end of oppression.
The Statue of Liberty has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1984.

teile.einleitung: El Niño is a climate phenomenon in the tropical Pacific. The sea water off South America becomes unusually warm, and this changes wind and weather in many parts of the world.
wichtigste: “El Niño” is Spanish and means the **Christ Child**.
El Niño arises in the tropical **Pacific**.
It occurs irregularly about every 2 to 7 years.
The **trade winds** become weaker in the process.
In Peru, El Niño often brings heavy rain.
Off Peru, fishermen then catch fewer fish.
A strong El Niño makes the Earth temporarily warmer.

abschnitte.text: Fishermen on the coast of Peru noticed long ago that the sea sometimes became warm around Christmas. They called this “El Niño”, which literally means “the boy” and refers to the **Christ Child**. Today experts use the name for the whole climate phenomenon. The cold opposite phase is called **La Niña**, “the girl”.

Normally the **trade winds** blow over the tropical Pacific from east to west. They push warm surface water towards Asia and Australia. Off South America, cold water rises from the depths in its place. This deep water is rich in **nutrients**, so there is a lot of plankton and many fish there.

In El Niño the trade winds become weaker. The warm water sloshes back to the east and settles off the coast of South America. Over the warm sea a lot of water evaporates, the moist air rises, and in the usually dry coastal areas of Peru there is **heavy rain** and flooding. In Indonesia and Australia, by contrast, it often becomes dry.

Because no more cold deep water rises, the nutrients are missing. The plankton declines, and fish such as **anchovies** find hardly any food. For the fishermen in Peru this means poor catches. Harvests in other countries can also suffer, because rain stays away there or falls too heavily.

In a strong El Niño, the Pacific gives off a lot of heat to the air. The average temperature of the whole Earth therefore rises temporarily. Years with a strong El Niño such as 2016 or 2024 were among the warmest years ever measured. One event usually lasts about a year, and then it cools down again.

gewusst: On average El Niño comes about every four years, but never in a fixed rhythm, which is why it is hard to predict long in advance.
With El Niño, a single ocean can change the weather on several continents at the same time.

teile.einleitung: Natural gas is a combustible gas found deep under the ground. It is used for heating, cooking, industry and generating electricity. Like crude oil, it is a **fossil fuel**.
wichtigste: Natural gas consists mainly of **methane**.
When burned it produces heat, water and **carbon dioxide**.
Natural gas formed over millions of years from dead living things.
**Russia** has the largest natural gas reserves in the world, followed by Iran and Qatar.
It is transported in **pipelines** or, liquefied, by ship.
Switzerland has to import almost all its natural gas.

abschnitte.text: Millions of years ago, tiny living things from the sea, above all **plankton**, sank to the seabed. They were covered by mud and rock. Under high pressure and great heat they turned very slowly into crude oil and **natural gas**. The gas collects in porous rock beneath a dense layer that does not let it escape. Because it takes so long for new natural gas to form, it counts as a **non-renewable** energy source.

Natural gas consists for the most part of **methane**, a compound of carbon and hydrogen. When burned it produces **heat**, water and **carbon dioxide** (CO2). Natural gas produces less CO2 than coal or heating oil, but still contributes to climate change. If methane gets into the air unburned, it is even a particularly strong **greenhouse gas**.

**Russia** has the largest proven natural gas deposits in the world, above all in **Siberia**. Next come **Iran** and **Qatar** (as of 2024). The USA, Norway and other countries also produce large amounts. Natural gas fields often lie under the seabed, and then it is produced with drilling platforms.

Natural gas is usually transported through long **pipelines**. For long journeys across the sea, it is cooled to about minus 162 degrees, when it becomes liquid and fits into special tankers as **LNG**. **Switzerland** does not produce any natural gas itself. It imports it through pipelines from neighbouring countries. So that a leak can be noticed, a **scent** that smells of rotten eggs is added to the gas, which is actually odourless.

gewusst: Natural gas is odourless by nature, and the typical gas smell is only added artificially.
Liquefied natural gas takes up about 600 times less space than gaseous.

teile.einleitung: A dune is a hill of sand piled up by the wind. Dunes are found in deserts, but also on many sea beaches. Some are as small as a heap of sand, others taller than a skyscraper.
wichtigste: A dune is a hill of sand.
The wind builds the dunes.
Dunes can migrate over time.
A crescent dune is also called a barchan and has the shape of a half moon.
On the side facing away from the wind, a dune is steeper.
In the Namib in Africa there are some of the highest dunes in the world.

abschnitte.text: Dunes form where there is a lot of loose **sand** and strong **wind**. The wind lifts the grains of sand and rolls or bounces them across the ground. When it meets an obstacle, such as a stone or a bush, the sand stays lying there. In this way a hill gradually grows. In deserts and on beaches there are no plants to hold the sand, so there are many dunes there.

A dune has two sides. The side from which the wind comes is called the **windward side**. It is gentle, and the wind pushes the sand up it. At the top the sand falls over the edge onto the other side, the **lee side**. The **side facing away from the wind** is therefore **steeper**. Because the wind constantly carries sand from front to back, dunes slowly **migrate** onwards. Some move several metres a year.

There are many different dune shapes. Particularly well known is the **crescent dune**, which is also called a **barchan**. It has the shape of a **half moon**. Its two tips point **in the direction of the wind**, because at the edges there is less sand, and it travels faster there. Crescent dunes form when the wind mostly blows from the same direction and there is not very much sand.

abschnitte.titel: Giant dunes in the desert and by the sea
abschnitte.text: In the **Namib** desert in the south-west of Africa stand some of the **highest dunes in the world**. Some are over 300 metres high and glow red because the sand contains iron. In Europe, the **Dune du Pilat** in **France** on the Atlantic is especially high, measuring about 100 metres. There are also many dunes on the **sea beaches** of the North Sea and the Baltic. There, marram grass is planted so that the sand does not blow away.

gewusst: When sand slides down a dune, a deep humming sound can sometimes be heard. This is called “singing dunes”.
There are sand dunes on Mars too, which can be seen clearly in pictures from space probes.

teile.einleitung: The emu is a large flightless bird from Australia. It cannot fly, but it is an excellent runner and, after the ostrich, the second tallest bird in the world.
wichtigste: The emu lives wild only in **Australia**.
It **cannot fly**, because it is too heavy and has small wings.
Only the **ostrich** grows bigger.
An emu grows almost 2 metres tall.
It runs at up to about 50 km/h.
In the emu, the **father** incubates the eggs.
Emu eggs are large and **dark green**.

abschnitte.text: The emu has only small wings that almost disappear under the feathers. It is far too heavy to fly. But it has long, strong legs. With them it reaches about **50 kilometres per hour**, as fast as a car in town. It can also run long distances and even swim.

A fully grown emu grows almost **two metres** tall and is therefore often taller than a person. Its feathers are brownish grey and look shaggy, almost like hair. This is good **camouflage** in dry grass. The neck and head have only a few feathers, and the skin there has a bluish shimmer.

The female lays large, **dark green** eggs. An emu egg weighs about as much as ten hen’s eggs. After that the **male** takes over: he sits on the eggs for about eight weeks and hardly eats in that time. When the striped chicks have hatched, the father protects and leads them for a long time.

Emus live in many parts of Australia, mainly in open landscapes such as grassland and scrub. They eat plants, fruit, seeds and insects. Together with the **kangaroo**, the emu holds the shield of Australia’s coat of arms. Both animals are found in the wild only there.

gewusst: In the emu’s feathers, two feathers always grow out of one quill, which is the case in hardly any other bird.

teile.einleitung: Globalisation means that countries and people all over the world are becoming more and more closely connected. Goods, money, information and people now travel faster and further than ever before. Your phone, your clothes or your bananas often come from many different countries.
wichtigste: Globalisation is the worldwide linking of the economy, politics, culture and communication.
The standard container of the 1950s cut transport costs in world trade particularly sharply.
TEU stands for Twenty-foot Equivalent Unit and measures the load of container ships.
ETH Zurich calculates the well-known KOF Index of Globalisation.
Offshoring means moving activities abroad.
Glocalisation means that global products are adapted locally.
The annual meeting of the World Economic Forum takes place in Davos.

abschnitte.text: **Globalisation** describes the growing interconnection of the world. Companies produce and sell in many countries, and news spreads in seconds over the internet. Music, films and food are also shared around the world. Globalisation is not new: the Silk Road already linked China with Europe over 2,000 years ago, but since about 1990 it has become much faster.

In the 1950s the American Malcom McLean invented the **standard container**, a steel box with standardised measurements. It can be loaded from a ship onto a lorry or train without being repacked, and this cut transport costs sharply. The load of container ships is measured in **TEU**, short for Twenty-foot Equivalent Unit, that is, one 20-foot container. The biggest ships today carry over 20,000 such containers.

Many companies move work to other countries, where wages are lower or specialists are available. This is called **offshoring**. So a T-shirt might have its cotton spun in India, be sewn in Bangladesh and be sold in Switzerland. At the same time, companies adapt their products to local tastes, which is called **glocalisation**. One example is fast-food chains that offer different menus in different countries.

The sociologist **Saskia Sassen** coined the term **global city**. It means cities such as New York, London or Tokyo, from which the world economy is steered. Banks, stock exchanges and the headquarters of big corporations are based there. Zurich and Geneva also play an important international role as financial and organisational centres.

Switzerland is one of the most globalised countries in the world. This is shown by the **KOF Index of Globalisation**, which is calculated by the economic research institute of ETH Zurich. Every year the World Economic Forum meets in **Davos**, where politicians and business people from all over the world hold discussions. The World Trade Organization (WTO) has its seat in Geneva.

Globalisation has brought more prosperity to many countries and made goods cheaper. Critics point to poor working conditions, environmental damage from long transport routes and growing inequality. In crises such as the coronavirus pandemic it became clear that worldwide **supply chains** are also vulnerable. That is why many people today pay attention to fair trade and regional products.

begriffe.erklaerung: Moving work or production to another country.
Worldwide products are adapted to local wishes.
A unit of measurement for a standard container 20 feet long.
All the steps and companies needed until a product is on the shop shelf.

gewusst: A large share of all goods in world trade is transported by ship.
The World Economic Forum was founded in 1971 and has met every January in Davos for decades.

teile.einleitung: The temperate zone is the climate zone in which Switzerland also lies. Typical are four clearly different seasons: a warm summer, a cold winter, and spring and autumn in between.
wichtigste: The temperate zone lies between the tropics and the polar regions.
Switzerland and Germany lie in the temperate zone.
There are four seasons: spring, summer, autumn and winter.
In winter there is often frost and snow, and January is usually the coldest month.
Many deciduous trees such as the beech lose their leaves in autumn.
Some animals such as the hedgehog hibernate.

abschnitte.text: The Earth is divided into **climate zones**. Around the Equator lie the hot **tropics**, and at the far north and south the cold **polar regions**. In between, on each half of the Earth, lies the **temperate zone**. There it is neither always hot nor always icy cold. The temperate zone includes large parts of Europe, including Switzerland, Germany and France, but also parts of North America and East Asia, for example.

Typical of the temperate zone are the **four seasons**. In **spring** it gets warmer, and the cherry trees and many other plants blossom. **Summer** is warm, sometimes hot, and there are often thunderstorms. In **autumn** the days become shorter and cooler. In **winter** there is often frost and snow. In Switzerland **January** is usually the coldest month.

In the temperate zone many **deciduous trees** grow, for example the **beech**, the oak and the maple. In autumn their leaves turn yellow, orange and red and fall off. In this way the trees lose less water in winter and are not damaged by the snow. In spring they put out new leaves. Conifers such as the spruce, by contrast, mostly stay green all year.

The animals have to cope with the cold winter. The **hedgehog** **hibernates**: its body cools down and its heart beats slowly, so it saves energy. Marmots also sleep through the winter. Squirrels lay in stores, and many migratory birds fly to warmer countries. Other animals grow a thicker winter coat.

Even within Switzerland the climate varies. In **Ticino** on the southern side of the Alps it is milder and sunnier. On the lakes such as Lake Maggiore and Lake Lugano, **palm trees** even grow outdoors, for example on the Brissago Islands. The mountains protect the area from cold winds from the north. In the high Alps, by contrast, it is cool all year round.

gewusst: The Chinese windmill palm that grows in Ticino originally comes from East Asia and can even stand light frost.
In hibernation a hedgehog can greatly slow its heartbeat and breathes only rarely.

teile.einleitung: The **Euphrates** is the longest river in Western Asia. Together with the Tigris it shaped Mesopotamia, where some of the oldest great civilisations in the world arose.
wichtigste: The Euphrates and the Tigris both rise in Turkey.
The Euphrates is longer than the Tigris.
The land between the two rivers is called **Mesopotamia**, which means “land between the rivers”.
The city of Raqqa in Syria lies on the Euphrates.
The great Atatürk Dam in Turkey holds back the Euphrates.
The Euphrates and the Tigris flow together and run into the Persian Gulf as the **Shatt al-Arab**.

abschnitte.text: The Euphrates rises in the highlands of **Turkey**, like the Tigris. It flows through **Syria** and **Iraq** to the south-east. At almost 3,000 kilometres it is clearly longer than the Tigris. In Syria the city of **Raqqa** lies on its bank. In the south of Iraq the Euphrates and the Tigris join to form the **Shatt al-Arab**, which runs into the Persian Gulf.

The area between the Euphrates and the Tigris is called **Mesopotamia**, “land between the rivers”. Here, over 5,000 years ago, the first cities and **cuneiform script** arose. Famous places such as **Babylon** and **Ur** lay on the Euphrates. The water of the rivers made farming possible in the dry region in the first place. For this reason it has always been important to people above all for the **irrigation** of fields.

For decades Turkey has been building the **Southeastern Anatolia Project**, a large programme of dams and irrigation systems on the Euphrates and Tigris. The centrepiece is the **Atatürk Dam** on the Euphrates, which was completed around 1990. When the reservoir was filled, less water flowed downstream. This led to disputes with **Syria** and **Iraq**, which also urgently need the water.

Dams supply electricity and water, but they also flood valleys and villages. A well-known example is **Hasankeyf** on the Tigris. The old town with its cave dwellings and buildings was largely flooded for the **Ilısu Dam**. Some valuable buildings were moved to a new site beforehand. Such projects are controversial because they bring benefits but also destroy cultural treasures and habitats.

gewusst: The Euphrates is mentioned in very old writings, including the Bible.
In the area where the Euphrates and Tigris meet the sea lie large marshes that are part of the UNESCO World Heritage.

teile.einleitung: The International Date Line is an imaginary line on the Earth where the date changes. Anyone who crosses it jumps a day forward or back. It runs mostly through the middle of the Pacific.
wichtigste: The Date Line roughly follows the 180th line of longitude.
It runs mostly through the Pacific.
Anyone who crosses it going west jumps a day forward.
It makes bends so that countries are not split, for example around Russia.
In 2011 Samoa skipped 30 December.
On Earth, up to three different calendar days can apply at the same time.

abschnitte.text: Because the Earth turns, it is not midday everywhere at the same time. Each time zone is roughly one hour ahead of the next. If you keep travelling further east, more and more hours are added. The day therefore has to change somewhere. This line is the **Date Line**. It roughly follows the **180th line of longitude**, exactly opposite the prime meridian at Greenwich.

The Date Line runs mostly through the **Pacific**, where few people live. It is not straight, however. In the far north it bends eastwards around **Russia**, so that the whole country lies on the same side. In the **Bering Strait** it runs between **Big Diomede and Little Diomede**. The two lie only about 4 kilometres apart but have different calendar days.

Some countries have switched sides to be better connected with their trading partners. The **Philippines** skipped a day at the end of 1844 and so moved to the Asian side. In 2011, **Samoa** dropped **30 December** to be closer to Australia and New Zealand. On the island of **Kiritimati**, New Year is celebrated in one of the first inhabited places on Earth.

abschnitte.titel: Around the World in Eighty Days
abschnitte.text: In the novel “Around the World in Eighty Days” by **Jules Verne**, **Phileas Fogg** travels east around the world. He believes he has just lost his bet. But because he crossed the Date Line, he gained a day on the way. So he arrives in time after all and wins the bet.

The time zones around the Date Line are spread very far apart. For this reason, for a short time **up to three** different calendar days can apply on Earth at the same time. When it is midday in Switzerland, it is already almost midnight on the other side of the Earth.

gewusst: The sailors on Magellan’s voyage around the world found on their return that a day was missing from their calendar.
On the Diomede Islands you can look from today across into tomorrow.

teile.einleitung: Edmund Hillary was a mountaineer and explorer from New Zealand. In 1953, together with the Sherpa Tenzing Norgay, he was the first to reach the summit of Mount Everest. Later he worked for many years for the people of Nepal.
wichtigste: Edmund Hillary came from New Zealand and first worked as a beekeeper.
In 1953 he and Tenzing Norgay were the first to stand on Mount Everest.
The expedition was organised by Britain.
After the success, Hillary was knighted.
In 1958 he reached the South Pole with converted tractors.
In 1985 he landed at the North Pole in an aeroplane with Neil Armstrong.
With the Himalayan Trust he built schools and hospitals in Nepal.

abschnitte.text: **Edmund Hillary** was born in 1919 in **New Zealand**. Together with his brother he worked as a **beekeeper** and kept bees. In his free time he climbed the mountains of the New Zealand Alps. Soon he also ventured onto the high peaks of the Himalaya. He died in 2008.

Before Hillary succeeded, many others tried. In **1952** a **Swiss expedition** was on Everest. The mountaineer **Raymond Lambert** from Geneva, together with Tenzing Norgay, got up to about **8,600 metres**. Then they had to turn back. The experience of the Swiss helped the next expedition find the best route.

abschnitte.titel: On the roof of the world
abschnitte.text: In **1953**, **Britain** organised a large expedition to **Mount Everest**. On 29 May, Edmund Hillary and the Sherpa **Tenzing Norgay** reached the summit. They were the first two people on the highest mountain on Earth. The news went round the world. For this Hillary was **knighted** by the British Queen and from then on was called Sir Edmund Hillary.

Hillary was also an explorer of the polar regions. In **1958** he reached the **South Pole** with a group, using converted **tractors**. In **1985** he landed at the **North Pole** in a small aeroplane together with **Neil Armstrong**, the first person on the Moon. So he stood on the highest mountain and at both poles of the Earth.

Hillary never forgot the people of the Himalaya. He founded the foundation **Himalayan Trust**. With it he built many **schools** and **hospitals** in Nepal, especially in the Sherpa region below Everest. For this he is still very popular in Nepal today. For many people this work was more important than his records.

gewusst: Hillary’s face is shown on the New Zealand five-dollar note.
On the summit of Everest, Hillary took a photo of Tenzing, but there is no photo of Hillary himself on the summit.

teile.einleitung: Enclaves and exclaves are areas that lie outside their own country and are surrounded by another state. Around Switzerland there are two well-known examples: **Büsingen** and **Campione d’Italia**.
wichtigste: From the point of view of the surrounding state, an area is an **enclave**.
From the point of view of the state it belongs to, it is an **exclave**.
**Büsingen am Hochrhein** is a German municipality completely surrounded by Switzerland.
**Campione d’Italia** is an Italian exclave on Lake Lugano.
**Lesotho** is a state completely surrounded by South Africa.
**Nakhchivan** belongs to Azerbaijan and is separated from the mainland by Armenia.

abschnitte.text: The words come from Latin: “en” means in and “ex” out. An **enclave** is a foreign area enclosed within one’s own country. An **exclave** is a part of one’s own country that lies outside. So it depends on the point of view. The former **Verenahof** near Schaffhausen was, until 1967, an enclave from the Swiss point of view and an exclave from Germany’s.

**Büsingen am Hochrhein** lies near Schaffhausen on the Rhine and is completely surrounded by Swiss territory. The municipality belongs to Germany but is attached to the **Swiss customs area**. For this reason there are no customs checks between Büsingen and Switzerland. In everyday life people mostly pay in **francs**, and there are both German and Swiss postcodes.

**Campione d’Italia** lies on the shore of **Lake Lugano** and is surrounded all round by the canton of Ticino. The place belongs to Italy. For a long time it was closely tied to Switzerland: people paid in francs and had Swiss telephone numbers. Since 2020, however, Campione has belonged to the **customs area of the European Union**. The place was known for its large casino.

Sometimes even a whole state is an enclave. **Lesotho** is completely surrounded by **South Africa** and lies everywhere over 1,000 metres above sea level. The **Vatican** and **San Marino** are also entirely enclosed by Italy. Eswatini, by contrast, is not a true enclave, because it also borders Mozambique.

**Nakhchivan** belongs to Azerbaijan but is separated from the mother country by Armenian territory. It borders Armenia, Iran and Turkey. The Spanish exclave **Llívia** lies in the French Pyrenees, with only a narrow strip separating it from Spain. In **Baarle-Hertog** in Belgium there are over twenty Belgian enclaves within the Dutch municipality of Baarle-Nassau. Between **India and Bangladesh**, over 160 enclaves were exchanged in 2015.

gewusst: In Baarle-Hertog the state border runs in places right through houses and shops.
Lesotho, the Vatican and San Marino are the only states in the world that are completely surrounded by a single other state.

teile.einleitung: In a **landslide**, earth, debris or rock slides down a slope. In a mountainous country like Switzerland this is an important natural hazard, and experts therefore monitor many slopes closely.
wichtigste: Most often, heavy or long-lasting rain triggers a landslide.
In 1806 a rockslide buried the village of Goldau in the canton of Schwyz.
A **debris flow** is a fast stream of water, mud and rock.
In 2017 debris flows hit the village of Bondo in the Bergell after a rockslide at Piz Cengalo.
In May 2025 Blatten in the Lötschental was largely buried by a glacier collapse.
When the **permafrost** in the Alps thaws, mountain slopes become less stable.

abschnitte.text: A slope stays in place as long as the ground holds firmly together. If it rains heavily or for a long time, the earth soaks up water, becomes heavy and slippery. Then it can start to slide. A distinction is made between slow **slides**, fast **debris flows** and **rockslides**, in which large masses of rock break off. A debris flow is a stream of water, mud and rock that shoots quickly down a stream bed.

In 1806 a mighty **rockslide** from the Rossberg buried the village of **Goldau** in the canton of Schwyz, and almost 500 people lost their lives. In 2017 a huge rockfall broke off at **Piz Cengalo**, and afterwards debris flows hit the village of **Bondo** in the Bergell. In May 2025 a collapse of the Birch Glacier largely buried the Valais village of **Blatten** in the Lötschental. Fortunately the residents had been brought to safety beforehand.

The Graubünden village of **Brienz/Brinzauls** lies on a slope that has been moving slowly down the valley for a long time. In 2023 a rockfall threatened, and the whole village had to be **evacuated**. Measuring devices monitor the mountain around the clock. In this way warnings can be given in good time. In Switzerland, **hazard maps** show where building is allowed and where protective structures are needed.
