wichtigste: A delta is more likely to form when a river brings a lot of material and the tides are weak.
A funnel-shaped estuary is also called an estuary proper.
The Elbe flows into the North Sea at Cuxhaven with a wide funnel-shaped estuary.
The wetland of the Camargue lies in the Rhône delta.
On Lake Maggiore, the Ticino forms the protected delta of the Bolle di Magadino.
The Volga forms the largest river delta in Europe.

abschnitte.text: A river carries **sand**, **gravel** and **mud** with it. At the mouth the water slows down and leaves this material behind. In this way the land slowly grows out into the water. The river splits into many channels. Because the Nile delta looks like a triangle from above, it was named after the Greek letter **delta**.

A **funnel-shaped estuary** becomes wider and wider towards the outside, like a funnel. The technical word for it is **estuary**. It forms when the **tides** are strong. Ebb and flow wash the material out to sea again and again, so that no delta can form. An example is the **Elbe**, which flows into the North Sea at **Cuxhaven**. The Thames in England also has a funnel-shaped estuary.

Whether a delta or a funnel-shaped estuary forms depends mainly on two things. If a river brings **a lot of material** and the **tides are weak**, a delta is more likely to grow. If the tides are strong, a funnel-shaped estuary is more likely to form. That is why there are many deltas on inland lakes and on seas with little ebb and flow, such as the Mediterranean.

The **Volga** forms the **largest river delta in Europe** on the Caspian Sea. In the Rhône delta in southern France lies the **Camargue**, a wetland with flamingos, white horses and rice fields. Deltas are important habitats for birds and fish. At the same time their soil is often very fertile.

There are also deltas on Swiss lakes. On **Lake Maggiore**, the river **Ticino** forms the **Bolle di Magadino**, a protected nature area with many birds. The Maggia has built up a large delta near Locarno, on which parts of Locarno and Ascona now stand. The Rhine forms a delta in Lake Constance.

gewusst: The largest delta in the world is formed by the Ganges and Brahmaputra in Bangladesh and India.
Because of the deposits of the Rhine, Lake Constance is slowly getting smaller.

teile.einleitung: Fracking is a method of getting natural gas and oil out of very dense rock. A liquid is forced down at high pressure so that fine cracks form.
wichtigste: In fracking, water, sand and additives are forced into the rock at high pressure.
The sand keeps the cracks open so that gas or oil can flow out.
Only horizontal drilling makes fracking in thin layers of shale economical.
Thanks to fracking, the USA has been the world’s largest crude oil producer since 2018.
In 2011 France became the first European country to ban fracking by law.
Fracking is controversial, among other things because of water and earthquakes.

abschnitte.text: The word comes from the English “hydraulic fracturing”. Gas and oil are often trapped in **shale**, a very dense rock. On their own they hardly flow to the well. A liquid is therefore forced in at high pressure, and fine **cracks** form. The **sand** mixed in serves as a propping agent so that the cracks stay open after the pressure is released.

Layers of shale are often only thin. For this reason drilling goes first vertically and then **horizontally** through the layer. This **horizontal drilling** brings a long section into contact with the rock. In this way fracking can be done at many points. Only this combination makes production economical. This is called **unconventional** gas and oil.

abschnitte.titel: The shale revolution in the USA
abschnitte.text: The pioneer is regarded as the Texan businessman **George P. Mitchell**. At the end of the 1990s he was able to produce shale gas economically in the Barnett Shale. After 2010, production in the USA rose sharply. Since 2018 the USA has been the **largest crude oil producer** in the world. Important are the **Permian Basin** in Texas and New Mexico and the **Bakken Formation** in North Dakota.

A shale well delivers a lot at the start. Already in the first year, though, it often loses a large part of its output. New wells therefore have to be drilled all the time to keep production up. This takes a lot of land, water and material.

Critics fear dangers to **groundwater** and the environment. In **Oklahoma**, small **earthquakes** increased sharply after 2009. The main cause is thought to be the injection of salty waste water into deep layers. Supporters stress cheap energy and independence from imports. **France** banned fracking in 2011, and in **Germany** unconventional fracking has been largely banned since 2017.

gewusst: The Permian Basin is named after the geological period called the Permian.
Part of the water that is injected in fracking comes back up as salty formation water.

teile.einleitung: A gated community is a closed residential area with walls, fences and guarded entrances. Only residents and their guests may enter. Such developments exist above all in America and South Africa.
wichtigste: Gated communities are closed residential areas with access control.
Streets and facilities are private.
A private owners’ association usually looks after security and upkeep.
Blakely and Snyder distinguished three types in 1997.
Well-known examples are Alphaville near São Paulo and Nordelta near Buenos Aires.
Critics say they increase social separation in cities.

abschnitte.text: A **gated community** is surrounded by **walls or fences** and has **guarded entrances**. Streets, parks and playgrounds are **private**. The owners pay fees to a **private management**. It organises security, roads and green spaces. Tasks that the local authority would otherwise take on are in this way done privately.

**Edward Blakely** and **Mary Gail Snyder** studied closed residential developments in the USA. In their book “Fortress America” of 1997 they distinguished three types. **Lifestyle communities** are geared to leisure, for example with a golf course or facilities for seniors. **Prestige communities** emphasise social status. With the third type, **security** is in the foreground.

In Brazil such developments are called **“condomínios fechados”**, and in Argentina **“barrios cerrados”**. From the 1970s, the development **Alphaville** with guarded residential districts, offices and shops grew up west of **São Paulo**. Near **Buenos Aires** lies **Nordelta** on the Río Luján. It is a private planned town with many guarded districts and lakes.

In Latin America and **South Africa**, residents especially often give **protection from crime** as the reason. In South Africa, many guarded developments, the **security estates**, arose after the end of apartheid, for example in Johannesburg. In addition, **prestige** and a particular **lifestyle** play a part. Peace and quiet and well-kept green spaces also attract people.

Gated communities separate well-off households spatially from the rest of the population. Experts speak of **social segregation**. The city breaks up into separate parts, which is called **fragmentation**. Supporters, by contrast, stress the right to security and to shape one’s own surroundings. In Europe, and also in Switzerland, such closed residential developments are much rarer.

gewusst: Some gated communities are so large that they have their own schools, shops and hospitals.
Segregation means that different groups of the population live separately from each other.

teile.einleitung: A river delta forms where a river flows into a sea or a lake and deposits sand, gravel and mud there. In this way new land grows out into the water.
wichtigste: A delta forms when a river deposits a lot of material at its mouth.
In a delta the river divides into several distributary channels.
In 1975 William Galloway classified deltas by river, waves and tides.
The Mississippi is known for its bird’s-foot delta.
In Switzerland the Maggia builds a delta into Lake Maggiore, and the Alpine Rhine one into Lake Constance.
The Danube Delta is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

abschnitte.text: A river carries stones, sand and mud with it. When it flows into calm water, it slows down and leaves the material behind. Over time a piece of land grows out into the sea or lake in this way. The river divides into several **distributary channels**. The delta gets its name from the Greek letter Δ, because the Nile Delta has roughly this shape.

The geologist **William Galloway** arranged deltas in a triangle in 1975. What matters is whether the **river supply, waves or tides** decide the shape. The **Mississippi Delta** is river-dominated: the river builds its arms with levees far out into the Gulf of Mexico, like a **bird’s foot**. The Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta, by contrast, is strongly shaped by the tides.

In lakes a **Gilbert delta** with three layers often forms. At the top lie flat **topset beds**. At the front follow steep **foreset beds**, because coarse material slides down the delta front. In front of them lie fine **bottomset beds** of mud.

The **Maggia** brings a lot of debris from the Maggia Valley and deposits it in **Lake Maggiore**. Parts of **Locarno and Ascona** now lie on this delta. The **Alpine Rhine** dumps large amounts of debris and sand into **Lake Constance** every year. Its delta therefore keeps growing out into the lake.

In the delta of the **Rhone** in southern France lies the **Camargue** with lagoons, salt meadows and flamingos. The **Danube Delta** on the Black Sea is one of the largest wetlands in Europe, and its Romanian part has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1991. On the **Nile**, the **Aswan High Dam** has held back the mud since the 1960s. Without fresh supplies, the Mediterranean wears away parts of the delta coast.

gewusst: Deltas are often very fertile, so many people live there.
Tributaries flow into a river, while distributary channels branch off from it.

teile.einleitung: A free trade agreement is a treaty between countries that remove tariffs and other trade barriers among themselves. In this way goods can be traded more easily and more cheaply.
wichtigste: In a free trade area the tariffs between the partners disappear.
Towards other countries, each member keeps its own tariffs.
Rules of origin lay down which goods are duty-free.
Switzerland and the then EEC concluded a free trade agreement in 1972.
EFTA was founded in 1960, and today its members are Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein.
In March 2021 the Swiss electorate narrowly approved the agreement with Indonesia.

abschnitte.text: A **tariff** is a fee that is paid when goods are brought in. In a **free trade area** these tariffs between the partner countries disappear. But each country keeps its **own tariffs towards third countries**. This is the difference from a **customs union** such as the EU: it additionally has a common external tariff. So that only genuine partner goods are duty-free, there are **rules of origin**. They determine how much of a product must have been made in the partner country.

**EFTA**, the European Free Trade Association, was founded in 1960 with the **Stockholm Convention**. Today its members are **Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein**. In 1972 Switzerland and the then **EEC** signed a free trade agreement for industrial goods. To this day it is an important basis for trade with the EU. The EEC itself had been founded in 1957 with the Treaties of Rome.

Switzerland has many further agreements, alone or together with EFTA, for example with **China** or **Japan**. A referendum was called against the agreement with **Indonesia**, mainly because of **palm oil**. In March 2021 it was approved with about 51.6 per cent Yes votes. On 1 October 2025 the EFTA agreement with **India** came into force. In it the EFTA states aim for investments of 100 billion US dollars within 15 years.

The agreement **CETA** between the EU and Canada has been provisionally applied since 2017. It removes almost all tariffs between the partners. In 2022 **RCEP** came into force. It includes the ten ASEAN states as well as China, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand. Measured by population, it is the largest free trade area in the world.

Supporters say that free trade makes goods cheaper and creates jobs in export firms. Critics fear disadvantages for farmers, the environment or working conditions. The economist **Jacob Viner** also distinguished **trade creation** and **trade diversion**. With diversion, people no longer buy from the cheapest supplier but from the duty-free partner.

gewusst: EFTA used to have more members, for example Britain and Austria, which later moved to the EU.
In Switzerland, a referendum can be called against international treaties such as free trade agreements.

teile.einleitung: In geography, deflation means the blowing away of sand and dust by the wind. The word comes from the Latin “deflare”, to blow away. In deserts especially, the wind shapes the landscape in this way.
wichtigste: Deflation is the blowing away of loose material by the wind.
The wearing away of rock by wind-driven grains of sand is called corrasion.
When the wind blows away everything fine, a layer of stones is left behind, called desert pavement.
A gravel or boulder desert is called a serir.
Blown-away Saharan dust sometimes turns snow in Switzerland reddish.
Loess is fine material deposited by the wind and forms fertile soils.

abschnitte.text: Where hardly any plants grow, the ground lies bare. The wind can then pick up fine **sand** and **dust** and carry it away. This is called **deflation**. Heavy stones stay where they are. **Corrasion** is something different: here, grains of sand driven by the wind grind away the rock, like a sandblaster.

If the ground consists of gravel and fine material, the wind gradually blows away everything fine. What is left is a dense layer of stones, the **desert pavement**. It protects the ground beneath it from further erosion. This often creates a gravel or boulder desert, which is called a **serir**. Large parts of the Sahara are not sand dunes at all but such stone and gravel deserts.

Over a very long time, the wind can blow out whole hollows. A well-known example is the **Qattara Depression** in Egypt. At its lowest point it lies over 100 metres below sea level. Deflation, together with other forces, helped to shape it.

The dust that is blown away can fly thousands of kilometres. Sometimes **Saharan dust** turns the sky yellowish and the **snow** in the Swiss Alps **reddish**. Where fine dust is deposited, **loess** forms. Loess is the counterpart of deflation and forms very **fertile soils**, for example in China and in parts of Central Europe.

In the **1930s**, an environmental disaster struck the Midwest of the USA, the **Dust Bowl**. Farmers had ploughed up the grassland, and then a long drought came. The wind blew huge amounts of topsoil away. Enormous dust storms darkened the sky, and many families had to leave their farms. Since then, fields have been protected from the wind with hedges and plant cover.

gewusst: On its way across the Atlantic, Saharan dust even fertilises the rainforest of the Amazon.
The word deflation is also used in economics, where it means that prices fall in general.

teile.einleitung: Kenya in East Africa uses the heat from the Earth’s interior on a large scale for electricity. The country has the largest installed geothermal capacity in the whole of Africa.
wichtigste: Kenya’s geothermal fields lie in the East African Rift.
The most important field is called Olkaria and lies by Lake Naivasha.
The power stations at Olkaria are run by the state company KenGen.
Kenya’s first geothermal power station went into operation in the 1980s.
In 2023 geothermal energy supplied about 40 to 50 per cent of Kenya’s electricity.
In 2023 Kenya had the largest geothermal capacity in Africa.

abschnitte.text: Through East Africa runs the **East African Rift**, a huge valley. Here parts of the Earth’s crust are slowly moving apart. As a result, hot rock rises closer to the surface, and there are volcanoes and hot springs. These are ideal conditions for using geothermal heat. Kenya has numerous geothermal fields in this area.

The country’s most important geothermal field is called **Olkaria**. It lies near **Lake Naivasha**, partly in Hell’s Gate National Park. The first power station there went into operation in the **1980s**. Since then many more plants have been built. Most of the power stations at Olkaria are run by the state company **KenGen**.

For a geothermal power station, deep holes are drilled into the hot ground. From these boreholes comes very hot water and **steam**. The steam flows through a **turbine** and turns it like a wind turbine. The turbine drives a **generator**, which produces electricity. The cooled water is often fed back into the ground.

In 2023 about **40 to 50 per cent** of Kenya’s electricity came from geothermal energy. A great advantage: geothermal heat supplies **baseload power**, that is, steady electricity, day and night and independent of the weather. This matters for Kenya, because hydroelectric power stations supply less electricity in times of drought. Kenya is therefore regarded in Africa as a model for clean energy.

Switzerland also wants to use more geothermal heat. In Switzerland, however, the hot rock lies much deeper than in Kenya. In **Basel** a project for electricity from geothermal heat was stopped in 2006 after it had triggered a noticeable **earthquake**. Today in Switzerland geothermal heat is used mainly for heating, with probes and heat pumps.

gewusst: In Hell’s Gate National Park, where part of Olkaria lies, you can see zebras and giraffes between the steam clouds of the power stations.
The East African Rift is thousands of kilometres long.

teile.einleitung: A doline is a funnel-shaped or bowl-shaped dip in the ground. It forms in karst areas, where the rock is slowly dissolved by water. Dolines are found all over the world, including in the Jura and in the Swiss Alps.
wichtigste: A doline is a funnel-shaped hollow in karst.
A distinction is made between solution dolines and collapse dolines.
Karst forms mainly in limestone, which water can dissolve.
If several dolines grow together, an uvala forms.
On the Yucatán Peninsula, water-filled collapse dolines are called cenotes.
The word doline comes from Slovenian.

abschnitte.text: Karst is a landscape made of rock that water can dissolve, above all **limestone**. Rainwater takes up some carbon dioxide from the air and the soil and becomes slightly acidic as a result. In this way it dissolves the limestone very slowly. The water quickly seeps away and flows on underground. In the process, caves and cracks form, and **dolines** form at the surface.

A **solution doline** forms when water dissolves the limestone especially strongly at one spot from above. The ground there gradually sinks into a funnel. A **collapse doline** forms when the roof of an underground cave falls in. It often has steep walls. If several dolines grow together, a larger hollow forms, which is called an **uvala**.

On the **Yucatán** Peninsula in Mexico there are many collapse dolines filled with clear groundwater. They are called **cenotes**. For the Maya they were important sources of water and sacred places. Today many cenotes are popular for swimming and diving, because some are linked by long underwater caves.

The word **doline** comes from **Slovenian** and means roughly valley. The Karst region between Slovenia and Italy gave its name to the whole type of landscape. In Switzerland, dolines can be found, for example, in the **Jura** and in limestone areas of the Alps. On walks you often see them as round hollows in pastures or woods.

gewusst: Dolines can be a few metres wide, but also several hundred metres wide.
Because water seeps away so quickly in karst, there are often hardly any streams on the surface.

teile.einleitung: Around the North Pole, several states are arguing over who owns which part of the sea floor. Because the ice is melting, mineral resources and new shipping routes in the Arctic are becoming ever more important.
wichtigste: Russia, Denmark and Canada claim the Lomonosov Ridge as part of their continental shelf.
In 2007 Russian submersibles planted a flag on the sea floor at the North Pole.
In 2022 Canada and Denmark divided up the small Hans Island.
The Arctic Council has eight member states.
Russia demands its own rules and permits for the Northern Sea Route.
Canada and the USA are arguing over the Northwest Passage.
The Svalbard Treaty of 1920 gives Norway sovereignty over Svalbard.

abschnitte.text: Under the UN **Convention on the Law of the Sea**, every coastal state may use an **economic zone** of 200 nautical miles off its coast. If the **continental shelf**, that is, the underwater continuation of the continent, reaches further out, a state can claim more sea floor. To do so it has to submit geological data to the **Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf**. The Commission examines the data and issues recommendations. The North Pole itself is owned by no state today.

The **Lomonosov Ridge** is an underwater mountain range that crosses the Arctic Ocean beneath the North Pole. Russia, Denmark (with Greenland) and Canada all say it is the natural extension of their continent. Their applications to the UN therefore overlap. A Russian expedition caused a stir in 2007: two submersibles planted a flag made of titanium on the sea floor at a depth of over 4,000 metres. Legally this has no significance, but it was a strong signal.

**Hans Island** is a small, bare island of rock between Greenland and Canada. For decades both sides claimed it. The dispute became known as the “Whisky War”, because visitors left flags and bottles of schnapps behind. In 2022 Canada and Denmark agreed peacefully and drew a border across the island. This is regarded as an example of how disputes in the Arctic can be settled.

As the sea ice retreats, two routes become more interesting. The **Northern Sea Route** runs along the Russian coast and greatly shortens the journey between Europe and East Asia. Russia demands registrations there and in some cases escort by icebreakers. The **Northwest Passage** runs through the islands in the north of Canada. Canada sees it as its own internal waters, whereas the USA sees it as an international strait through which all ships may pass freely.

In the **Arctic Council**, eight states work together: Canada, Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Russia, Sweden and the USA. In addition there are representatives of Indigenous peoples and observers, since 2017 including Switzerland. A special case is **Svalbard** (Spitsbergen). The **Svalbard Treaty** of 1920 gives Norway sovereignty over the islands. Citizens of all the treaty states, Switzerland included, may nevertheless carry on economic activity there.

gewusst: On Svalbard there is the seed vault, in which seeds of crop plants from all over the world are safely stored.
The dispute over Hans Island lasted about 50 years and ended entirely without violence.

teile.einleitung: **Fiji** is an island state in the South Pacific. It consists of over 300 islands with sandy beaches, volcanic mountains and colourful coral reefs.
wichtigste: Fiji lies in the Pacific and consists of over 300 islands.
The capital is called **Suva**, and the largest island **Viti Levu**.
In 1970 Fiji became independent from Britain.
The 180th line of longitude runs through the island group.
Many Indo-Fijians have ancestors from India.
In 2016 Fiji won its first Olympic gold medal, in rugby sevens.

abschnitte.text: Fiji lies in the middle of the **Pacific**, north of New Zealand. The state consists of **over 300 islands**, of which only some are inhabited. The largest island is called **Viti Levu**. The capital, **Suva**, is also there. Around the islands, large **coral reefs** grow under the water, where colourful fish live. That is why many divers and holidaymakers come to Fiji.

The **180th line of longitude** runs through the island group of Fiji. Near it lies the **Date Line**, where a new calendar day begins. So that the whole of Fiji lies in the same day, the Date Line makes a bend there. Fiji is therefore among the first countries in the world to celebrate the new year.

Fiji was for a long time a British **colony** and became independent from **Britain** in 1970. From the end of the 19th century the British brought many workers from **India** to the islands to work in the sugar cane fields. Their descendants are called **Indo-Fijians**. Today they live in the country together with the native Fijians. Besides English, Fijian and Hindi are also spoken.

A lot of **sugar cane** is grown in Fiji, from which sugar is obtained. Besides sugar, **tourism** is very important for the economy. The great passion of the Fijians is **rugby**. In 2016 in Rio, Fiji won its first Olympic gold medal in **rugby sevens**. The whole country celebrated, and there was even a public holiday.

gewusst: After the Olympic victory of 2016, Fiji issued a banknote with a picture of the rugby team.
Many of Fiji’s islands arose from volcanoes.

teile.einleitung: A river is a larger, natural body of water that flows constantly in one direction. It begins at a source and ends at its mouth in a sea, a lake or another river. So many large rivers rise in Switzerland that it is called the water tower of Europe.
wichtigste: A river is a flowing body of water that is larger than a stream.
The place where a river rises is called the source.
The place where it ends is called the mouth.
The Rhine flows through Basel.
The Rhone flows into the Mediterranean.
The Aare flows through the city of Bern.
The longest rivers on Earth are the Nile and the Amazon.

abschnitte.text: A **river** is a natural body of water that always flows downhill. Small watercourses are called streams, and very large ones are also called a great river. A river gets its water from rain, melted snow, glaciers and springs. The whole area from which water reaches a river is called its **catchment area**.

Every river begins at a **source**, for example at a glacier or a mountain lake. In its upper course it flows fast and cuts deep valleys into the rock. In its lower course it becomes wider and slower and forms loops called meanders. At the **mouth** it flows into a sea, a lake or a larger river, and sometimes it forms a delta there.

The **Rhine** rises in Graubünden, flows through Lake Constance and through Basel, and runs into the North Sea in the Netherlands. The **Rhone** comes from the Rhone Glacier in Valais, flows through Lake Geneva and runs into the Mediterranean in France. The Aare flows through Bern and is the longest river that runs entirely within Switzerland. The Inn carries water from the Engadine into the Danube and on to the Black Sea.

abschnitte.titel: The biggest rivers in the world
abschnitte.text: The **Nile** in Africa and the **Amazon** in South America are the two longest rivers on Earth, both over 6,000 kilometres long. The Amazon carries by far the most water. In Asia the Yangtze and the Mekong are especially long. The longest river in Europe is the Volga in Russia.

For thousands of years people have built their cities on rivers, because there are water, fish and fertile land there. Goods are carried on rivers by ship, and Basel even has a port on the Rhine. In Switzerland many **hydroelectric power stations** on rivers produce electricity. In summer, swimming in the Aare or the Rhine is very popular.

In rivers live fish such as trout, grayling and salmon, as well as insect larvae, beavers and water birds. In the past many rivers were straightened and squeezed into canals. Today in Switzerland many stretches are being **restored to a natural state**, so that animals and plants have more room again. This also protects against floods, because the river has more space to spread out.

begriffe.erklaerung: The place where a river rises from the ground or a glacier.
The place where a river flows into another body of water.
A river that flows into a larger river.
The whole area from which water reaches a river.
A large loop in a river.

gewusst: From Switzerland, water flows into four seas: the North Sea, the Mediterranean, the Adriatic and the Black Sea.
At the Rhine Falls near Schaffhausen, the Rhine plunges over 20 metres.

teile.einleitung: The catchment area of a river is the whole area from which water flows into it. Every raindrop that falls there ends up sooner or later in this river. Switzerland is especially interesting because several of Europe’s large catchment areas begin here.
wichtigste: The catchment area includes all the land that drains into a river.
The boundary between two catchment areas is called a watershed.
With about 7 million km², the Amazon has the largest catchment area in the world.
In Europe the Volga has the largest catchment area.
The catchment area of the Rhine measures about 185,000 km².
About two thirds of Switzerland drain via the Rhine into the North Sea.
Areas with no outflow to the sea are called endorheic areas.

abschnitte.text: A river gets its water not only from its source. Rain, snow and groundwater from a huge area flow to it through streams and tributaries. This whole area is called the **catchment area**. The boundary line between two neighbouring catchment areas is called a **watershed**. It usually runs along mountain ridges or the backs of hills. If a drop falls on one side, it flows into a different river from a drop on the other side.

The **Amazon** in South America has the **largest catchment area in the world**. It measures about **7 million km²**, which is about 170 times the area of Switzerland. In **Europe**, the **Volga** in Russia has the largest catchment area. The catchment area of the **Rhine** is about **185,000 km²**. It stretches from the Swiss Alps to the Netherlands.

abschnitte.titel: Water with no way to the sea
abschnitte.text: Not all water reaches the sea. In some areas the rivers flow into a lake with no outlet or seep away in the desert. This is called an **endorheic area**. The biggest example is the area around the **Caspian Sea**, into which the Volga also flows. Because a lot of water evaporates there, the water in such lakes is often salty.

Switzerland is often called the **water tower of Europe**. Its water flows into four seas. **About two thirds** of the area drain via the **Rhine** into the **North Sea**. The Rhône brings water to the Mediterranean, and the Inn, by way of the Danube, to the Black Sea. The Ticino flows via the Po into the Adriatic. The water from the **Val Müstair** in Graubünden also reaches the Adriatic, by way of the **Adige**.

At the **Witenwasserenstock** in the Alps, the catchment areas of the **Reuss**, the **Rhône** and the **Ticino** meet. The water on one side flows into the North Sea, on the second into the Mediterranean and on the third into the Adriatic. At the **Lunghin Pass** in the Engadine there is also such a triple watershed between the Rhine, the Po and the Danube. Such places show nicely how mountains share out the water.

gewusst: At the Lunghin Pass it is decided whether a raindrop flows into the North Sea, the Mediterranean or the Black Sea.
The federal experts monitor the amount of water in Swiss rivers at many measuring stations.

teile.einleitung: The Earth is a huge ball floating freely in space. Over 2,000 years ago clever people found proof of this, and today photos from space show its round shape quite clearly.
wichtigste: The Earth has the shape of a ball that is slightly flattened at the poles.
A small model of the Earth is called a **globe**.
At the equator, the way round the Earth measures about 40,000 kilometres.
Gravity holds all people on the ball, wherever they stand.
The first voyage by ship round the Earth began in 1519 under Ferdinand Magellan.
The Earth’s axis is tilted, so the axis of a globe is also tilted.

abschnitte.text: A **globe** is a small ball on which all the countries, seas and continents are shown. Unlike a flat map, it shows the Earth in its true shape. When a globe stands normally, the **North Pole** is at the top, because on globes and maps north is usually at the top. The axis of the globe is tilted because the real **Earth’s axis** is also tilted by about 23 degrees. In this way you can see clearly on a globe how the Earth lies in space.

When a ship comes across the sea from far away, you first see the **tip of the mast** and only later the hull. This is due to the **curvature** of the Earth’s surface. A second proof appears in a **lunar eclipse**: then the Earth’s shadow falls on the Moon, and its edge is always round. Only a ball throws a round shadow from every direction. Today we also see the round Earth in photos from satellites and space stations.

Many children wonder why the people on the “underside” of the Earth do not fall into space. The answer is **gravity**. The Earth pulls everything towards its centre. So for every person on the ball, “down” is where the ground is. In Australia people stand just as safely as we do in Switzerland.

Anyone who keeps travelling straight east will eventually arrive back at the starting point, because a ball has no edge. The first journey round the Earth began in 1519 under **Ferdinand Magellan**. He died on the way, but one ship returned to Spain in 1522. The way round the Earth at the **equator** is about 40,000 kilometres long. An aeroplane needs about two days for this distance without a break.

gewusst: The Greek scholar Eratosthenes calculated the circumference of the Earth astonishingly accurately over 2,200 years ago.
The oldest surviving globe was built in Nuremberg in 1492 and is called the “Erdapfel”, or earth apple.

teile.einleitung: El Tatio is a large geyser field in the north of Chile, in the Andes on the edge of the Atacama Desert. It lies at about 4,300 metres and is among the highest geyser fields in the world.
wichtigste: El Tatio lies in the north of Chile in the Andes.
The geyser field lies at about 4,300 metres above sea level.
There are many **geysers** and hot springs there.
In the early morning especially many columns of steam can be seen.
Many visitors come from the town of San Pedro de Atacama.

abschnitte.text: A **geyser** is a hot spring that again and again shoots water and steam into the air. Underground lies hot rock that comes from volcanoes. It heats the groundwater until it suddenly shoots upwards. In El Tatio there are very many such springs close together, as well as bubbling mud pots and steaming holes.

Visitors usually set off in the middle of the night so that they arrive at sunrise. Then the air is icy cold, often far below zero. The warm steam cools quickly in the cold air and becomes visible as a white cloud. When the sun is higher and the air becomes warmer, the columns of steam are much harder to see.

The water in the springs is boiling hot, and the ground can be thin. You must therefore stay on the paths. Because of the great height the air is thin, and many people feel **altitude sickness**. Anyone who walks slowly and drinks a lot usually feels better.

gewusst: El Tatio lies even higher than the Jungfraujoch, the highest railway station in Europe.
Nearby is the Atacama, one of the driest deserts on Earth, and yet it steams and bubbles everywhere in El Tatio.

teile.einleitung: Dolphins are intelligent marine mammals. They live in groups, communicate with whistles and find their prey with sound. Although they look like fish, they breathe air.
wichtigste: Dolphins are mammals and breathe through a blowhole.
They find their prey with clicking sounds and their echo.
When sleeping, only one half of the brain rests at a time.
Dolphins mostly live in groups.
The orca is the largest dolphin.
The best-known species is the bottlenose dolphin.
Some dolphins live in large rivers.

abschnitte.text: Dolphins belong to the **toothed whales**. They are **mammals** and not fish. That is why they have to come to the surface to breathe. They breathe through the **blowhole** on top of the head. When swimming, they move their tail fin **up and down**, whereas fish move their tail fin from side to side.

In murky water you often cannot see far. Dolphins therefore send out **clicking sounds** and listen for the **echo**. This is how they tell where a fish or an obstacle is. This is called **echolocation**. Bats find their way in a similar manner in the air.

Dolphins mostly live in **groups**, which are called pods. They hunt together and help each other. Each dolphin has its own **signature whistle**, a kind of name. The animals use it to call each other. Dolphins are regarded as very intelligent and playful.

Even in its sleep, a dolphin has to remember to surface to breathe. That is why only **one half of the brain** sleeps at a time, while the other stays awake. One eye is often open as it does so. After a while the two halves swap over.

The best-known species is the **bottlenose dolphin**. The largest dolphin is the **orca**, also called the killer whale. It can grow much bigger than a car. Besides the sea, some dolphins also live **in large rivers**, for example in the Amazon in South America. These river dolphins have a long, narrow snout.

gewusst: The orca is also called the killer whale but belongs to the dolphin family.
With their echolocation, dolphins can even detect fish buried in the sand.

teile.einleitung: Gabriela Mistral was a poet and teacher from Chile. In 1945 she became the first person from Latin America to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature.
wichtigste: Gabriela Mistral came from Chile.
Her real name was Lucila Godoy Alcayaga.
She worked as a teacher for a long time.
In 1945 she became the first person from Latin America to receive the Nobel Prize in Literature.
She is pictured on a Chilean banknote.

abschnitte.text: Gabriela Mistral was born in 1889 in the north of Chile. Her real name was **Lucila Godoy Alcayaga**. She chose the name **Gabriela Mistral** as a pen name. Already as a young woman she worked as a **teacher**, later also as a school head. The education of children was very important to her. In Mexico too she helped to set up schools.

Mistral wrote **poems** about love, grief, nature and the lives of ordinary people. Many of her texts are about **children**, and she also wrote lullabies. Her language is clear and full of feeling. Later she worked as a **consul**, that is, as a representative of Chile, in various countries.

In 1945 Gabriela Mistral received the **Nobel Prize in Literature**. She was the **first person from Latin America** to get this prize. She died in 1957 in the USA. In Chile she is still greatly revered today. She is pictured on a **Chilean banknote**.

gewusst: Only a few years after her, another poet from Chile, Pablo Neruda, received the Nobel Prize in Literature.

teile.einleitung: France is Switzerland’s western neighbour and, by area, the largest state in the European Union. The capital Paris with the Eiffel Tower is among the most visited cities in the world. French is also spoken in western Switzerland, the Romandie.
wichtigste: France lies to the west of Switzerland.
The capital is Paris, where the Eiffel Tower stands.
The flag of France has three vertical stripes in blue, white and red.
By area, France is the largest country in the European Union.
About 68 million people live in France (as of 2024).
Mont Blanc on the border with Italy is the highest mountain in the Alps.
The French Revolution of 1789 changed the whole of Europe.

abschnitte.text: France lies in the west of Europe and borders Switzerland in the east, among other places along the **Jura** and around Geneva. It has coasts on the Atlantic, on the English Channel and on the Mediterranean. In the south the Pyrenees form the border with Spain, and in the east lie the Alps with **Mont Blanc**. The longest river that flows entirely within France is the Loire.

**Paris** is the capital and by far the largest city in France. The **Eiffel Tower** was built for the World’s Fair of 1889 by the engineer Gustave Eiffel and is about 330 metres high. Other sights are the Louvre with the painting of the Mona Lisa, the cathedral of Notre-Dame and the Arc de Triomphe. Other large cities are Marseille, Lyon and Toulouse.

The flag of France is called the **Tricolour** and has three vertical stripes in blue, white and red. It dates from the time of the **French Revolution** of 1789, when the people rose up against the king. The motto of the country is “Liberty, Equality, Fraternity”. Later Napoleon Bonaparte ruled as emperor and conquered large parts of Europe, and in 1798 his troops also marched into Switzerland.

In France people speak **French**, which is also one of the national languages of Switzerland. France is famous for its cuisine with baguettes, croissants, many kinds of cheese and wine. Every summer the **Tour de France** takes place, one of the best-known cycle races in the world. Famous French people include the writer Victor Hugo and the scientist Marie Curie, who was born in Poland.

France is one of Switzerland’s most important trading partners. Every day a great many **cross-border commuters** come from France to work in Geneva, Basel or the Jura. Basel-Mulhouse airport lies on French soil but is run jointly by both countries. Lake Geneva and the Doubs also lie partly on the border.

Besides Paris, the châteaux on the Loire and the monastery island **Mont-Saint-Michel** are very well known. On the Côte d’Azur on the Mediterranean, many people go on holiday. In Chamonix you can take a cable car almost up to Mont Blanc. France is one of the most visited destinations in the world.

begriffe.erklaerung: A flag with three colours, which is what the French flag is called.
The French-speaking part of Switzerland.
People who live in one country and work in the neighbouring country.
The uprising from 1789 that broke the power of the king.

gewusst: The Eiffel Tower was originally supposed to be taken down again after 20 years.
France also includes territories far away from Europe, for example French Guiana in South America and the island of La Réunion in the Indian Ocean.

teile.einleitung: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is a huge country in Central Africa. It has large rainforests, the mighty Congo River and many mineral resources. By area it is the second largest country in Africa.
wichtigste: The capital is Kinshasa.
From 1971 to 1997 the country was called Zaire.
It is the second largest country in Africa.
The sea coast is only about 40 kilometres long.
Most of the world’s cobalt is mined here.
Lubumbashi in the south is the centre of mining in Katanga.
Virunga National Park is the oldest national park in Africa.

abschnitte.text: After Algeria, the **Democratic Republic of the Congo** is the **second largest country in Africa**. It is more than fifty times as big as Switzerland. Even so, its **sea coast** is only about **40 kilometres** long. The capital, **Kinshasa**, lies on the Congo River, directly opposite Brazzaville, the capital of the Republic of the Congo. The official language is French.

The area was for a long time a colony, first owned by the Belgian king and then by the state of **Belgium**. During this time the population suffered badly under forced labour. The country became independent in **1960**. From **1971 to 1997** it was called **Zaire** and was ruled by a dictator. Even after that, there were long wars and conflicts, above all in the east.

The DR Congo is rich in mineral resources such as copper, diamonds and **cobalt**. Cobalt is needed for **batteries** in mobile phones and electric cars. Most of the world’s cobalt is mined here. The centre of mining is the city of **Lubumbashi** in the Katanga region. However, many people in the country hardly benefit from this wealth.

The Congo River is one of the rivers with the most water in the world, and the rainforest is the second largest after the Amazon. In the east lies **Virunga National Park**, the oldest national park in Africa. Rare **mountain gorillas** live there. Near the city of **Goma** stands the volcano **Nyiragongo**, in whose crater lies a bubbling **lava lake**.

gewusst: Kinshasa and Brazzaville lie directly opposite each other, separated only by the Congo River.
In the Congo Basin lives the bonobo, a close relative of the chimpanzee that is found only in this country.

teile.einleitung: An **enclave** is an area that is completely surrounded by another state. If it belongs to a foreign country, from that country’s point of view it is an **exclave**. In the world there are many astonishing examples.
wichtigste: Whether it is an enclave or an exclave depends on the point of view.
From the surrounding state it is an enclave, from the mother country an exclave.
**Jungholz** in Tyrol can be reached by car only through Germany.
The **Verenahof** near Schaffhausen came to Switzerland in 1967.
**Llívia** is a Spanish village in the middle of France.
In 2015 India and Bangladesh exchanged over 160 enclaves.
In **Baarle** the border even runs through houses.

abschnitte.titel: A question of point of view
abschnitte.text: Imagine a small piece of land that belongs to state A but is surrounded all round by state B. For state A it is an **exclave**, a part that lies outside. For state B it is an **enclave**, a foreign area in its interior. The same area is therefore both at once. So the German village of Büsingen is an enclave from the Swiss point of view and an exclave from Germany’s.

The Tyrolean municipality of **Jungholz** is connected to Austria only at a single point, the summit of the Sorgschrofen. By car it can be reached only through German territory, and this is called a **functional exclave**. Near Schaffhausen there used to be the **Verenahof**, a few German houses on Swiss soil. With the state treaty on Büsingen it was handed over to Switzerland in 1967.

**Llívia** is a Spanish village in the Pyrenees that is surrounded all round by France. After the Peace of the Pyrenees in the 17th century, Spain had to give up villages, but Llívia counted as a town and stayed Spanish. In **Baarle** the Belgian municipality of Baarle-Hertog and the Dutch Baarle-Nassau lie interlocked. For some houses, the position of the front door decides which state they belong to.

The **Musandam** peninsula on the Strait of Hormuz belongs to Oman. Between it and the rest of Oman lies territory of the **United Arab Emirates**. **Nakhchivan** belongs to Azerbaijan but is separated from the mainland by Armenian territory. It borders Armenia, Iran and Turkey and is an autonomous republic.

The most complicated border tangle in the world long existed between **India and Bangladesh** in the area around Cooch Behar. There, enclaves lay inside enclaves, and there was even an enclave of the **third order**: an Indian field in a piece of Bangladesh that lay in India, which in turn lay in Bangladesh. In 2015 the two states exchanged over 160 enclaves. The residents changed their nationality or moved.

gewusst: The only third-order enclave in the world was a small field and disappeared with the exchange in 2015.
In Baarle even some shops and houses are divided by the border, which is marked as a line on the ground.

teile.einleitung: Development cooperation means that richer countries help poorer countries to reduce poverty in the long term. It is about education, health, clean water, agriculture and a working economy. In Switzerland the bodies mainly responsible are the **SDC** and **SECO**.
wichtigste: The **SDC** belongs to the Federal Department of Foreign Affairs (FDFA).
**SECO** is responsible for economic development cooperation.
According to the UN target, rich countries should spend **0.7 per cent** of their gross national income.
The OECD’s **DAC** decides what counts as official development assistance.
With **tied aid**, purchases must be made in the donor country.
**Helvetas** was founded in Zurich in 1955.
Development cooperation works in the long term, while humanitarian aid saves lives in emergencies.

abschnitte.text: The **Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation**, SDC for short, belongs to the FDFA, the foreign ministry of the federal government. It supports projects in partner countries, for example for schools, health or water. The **State Secretariat for Economic Affairs**, SECO for short, promotes trade, private firms and good economic policy in partner countries. How much money is available is decided by **Parliament** for several years at a time.

In 1970 the UN decided that rich countries should spend **0.7 per cent** of their **gross national income** (GNI) on development aid. GNI is the value of all the incomes earned by the residents of a country in a year. An example: with a GNI of 800 billion francs, that would be 800 billion times 0.007, so **5.6 billion francs**. Only a few countries reach the target permanently.

What counts as **official development assistance** (ODA) is decided by the Development Assistance Committee **DAC** of the OECD. It also regularly reviews the donor countries. **Tied aid** is viewed critically: the partner country then has to buy goods or services from the donor country, which often makes the aid more expensive. The **Paris Declaration** of 2005 stresses **ownership**: partner countries should decide their strategies themselves, and donors follow them.

Besides the federal government, many private organisations work in development cooperation. **Helvetas** was founded in 1955 in Zurich as the “Swiss aid organisation for non-European areas” and is among the first private Swiss organisations of this kind. It has had its present name since 1965. The aid organisations collect donations and often work closely with people on the ground.

abschnitte.titel: In the long term, not only in emergencies
abschnitte.text: **Humanitarian aid** is used after disasters or in wars and is meant to save lives at once, for example with food, tents and medicines. **Development cooperation**, by contrast, lasts many years. It aims to tackle the causes of poverty and improve structures, for example schools, hospitals or a reliable administration. Whether and how much aid makes sense is judged differently again and again in politics.

gewusst: The 0.7 per cent target is over 50 years old and is still reached regularly by only a few countries.
At its founding Helvetas was one of the first private organisations in Switzerland to help in the long term in countries outside Europe.
